reviews.name: AFFiNE
reviews.verdict: Pilot AFFiNE if combining documents and visual planning would improve your workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a source build already verified by our sandbox Buyers seeking measured evidence about synchronization reliability, recovery or production performance Operators treating the development dependency footprint as a production sizing recommendation

reviews.name: invoice-builder
reviews.verdict: Our Invoice Builder setup used 1,054 MB and built in 10 seconds, but its test process failed because the sqlite3 binary required GLIBC 2.38 even though all 4 executed tests passed.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that need a vendor-backed compliance guarantee: the README claims standards-compliant exports, but adopters still need to validate files against their jurisdiction and delivery network.

reviews.name: signal-cli-rest-api
reviews.verdict: Use signal-cli-rest-api if HTTP is the interface your application needs and you can maintain the account state and receiving workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need evidence of production message delivery from this review Operators who cannot maintain persistent account state Applications whose receiving workflow has not been tested through consumer disconnects and restarts Matrix users whose actual requirement is a conversation bridge…

reviews.name: OpenBot
reviews.verdict: OpenBot has one of the more convincing designs for giving agents real access without treating trust as a prompt-writing exercise.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive production teams that need a settled release today: the README labels OpenBot alpha, and an open issue shows that an allowed agent URL can redirect to an address the initial safety check would refuse.

reviews.name: bookorbit
reviews.verdict: BookOrbit merits a trial with copied books for its documented web, Kobo, and KOReader workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs verified device synchronization, playback, migration, or production deployment before choosing a server.

reviews.name: openflight
reviews.verdict: Our OpenFlight run installed 58 packages in 27 seconds, built in 8 seconds, and passed 1,341 tests, so the software deserves a trial if you are prepared to build the hardware.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who want a finished appliance: our 58-package install covered only software, while the roughly $400 build still needs assembly and radar setup.

reviews.name: filestash
reviews.verdict: Our Filestash build passed in 21 seconds, but all 109 Go packages failed during the 172-second test step, so source adopters do not have a clean baseline from our run.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who cannot test destructive file operations: open issue 994 reports WebDAV folder deletion on S3 also deleting a sibling with the same prefix, and the related fix remains an open pull request.

reviews.name: planka
reviews.verdict: Our PLANKA source install failed after 39 seconds during the server's Python virtual-environment setup, so the build and tests never ran.
reviews.skip_if: Agencies or consultants inviting paying clients into a Community instance: the license guide says third-party access in a commercial relationship requires Pro or Enterprise.

reviews.name: Antigravity-Manager
reviews.verdict: Our Antigravity Tools run built in 31 seconds, but it installed 817 packages, exposed no test target, and carried 22 known vulnerabilities, so we would keep it on one operator's trusted machine.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial adopters expecting an MIT or Apache license: the repository uses CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, which restricts licensed use to noncommercial purposes.

reviews.name: flexprice
reviews.verdict: Flexprice merits a shadow evaluation when you need usage pricing, credits, and entitlements alongside existing payment systems.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose existing payment-provider integration already handles their pricing without additional billing logic.

reviews.name: cal.diy
reviews.verdict: Try cal.diy only as a personal, non-production instance you can maintain yourself.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial or production scheduling: the maintainers direct those users to Cal.com.

reviews.name: InsForge
reviews.verdict: Trial InsForge if agent control over backend administration justifies maintaining the stack.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking measured application throughput, database scaling or production reliability; our run established none of these.

reviews.name: pangolin
reviews.verdict: Trial Pangolin if you need its documented combination of browser access and private resource access.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a demonstrated successful source build at commit 7319bf8.

reviews.name: cal.diy
reviews.verdict: Cal.diy is worth evaluating for a technically capable person who accepts its personal, non-production scope.
reviews.skip_if: Businesses seeking commercial scheduling infrastructure: the maintainers direct those users to Cal.com.

reviews.name: how-to-live-better
reviews.verdict: Our how-to-live-better run installed 35 packages in 18 seconds and built successfully in 5 seconds, making regeneration approachable for a reader that already ships as HTML.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need English documentation or an English interface: this edition's README and reading controls are Chinese.

reviews.name: Search
reviews.verdict: Search did not run in our Debian sandbox because its Swift ecosystem was unsupported and it had no Dockerfile, so our recommendation is a documented-feature trial rather than a verified runtime endorsement.
reviews.skip_if: People who need tabs, history, and passwords synchronized between devices: the README explicitly excludes sync and cloud accounts.

reviews.name: JIZURA
reviews.verdict: Our JIZURA run installed 1 package in 5 seconds, but skipped build and tests, so the easy developer setup comes without evidence of a working finished export.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a verified After Effects handoff: the guide describes mock-environment checks, and open issue 40 reports color and tracking warnings in the real panel.

reviews.name: shapeshift
reviews.verdict: Our Shapeshift run passed all 172 tests and built in 24 seconds, but installation brought 947 packages and a 765 MB footprint for a browser-local utility.
reviews.skip_if: People who need synchronized, backed-up task records: the README stores saved cards in browser localStorage.

reviews.name: deskworlds
reviews.verdict: Our Deskworlds run added 0 packages, used 89 MB, and passed its test command in 22 seconds, but the native wallpaper still requires macOS 13 and a source install.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users seeking a desktop wallpaper installer: only the browser scenes run there.

reviews.name: yeti
reviews.verdict: Keep Yeti on a pinned evaluation track until its artifact status is clear and you have reproduced the test outcome.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a released npm artifact: the supplied installation guide explicitly says none is available yet.

reviews.name: hit-and-run-web
reviews.verdict: Our run passed all 135 tests in 12 seconds after a 9-second install, but the checkout itself occupied 1,228.7 MB and the project still lacks a full campaign playthrough.
reviews.skip_if: Hosts that need uncomplicated rights to every shipped file: the license covers original project code but explicitly excludes The Simpsons: Hit & Run artwork, characters, audio, scripts, and game data.

reviews.name: clay-safari
reviews.verdict: Our Clay Safari run installed 21 packages in 9 seconds and produced a successful build in 10 seconds, making it an unusually approachable 3D code study despite the absent test target.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need full English contributor documentation: most of the 10,279-byte README, including setup details, is in Chinese.

reviews.name: shadcn-admin
reviews.verdict: Our shadcn-admin install stopped after 11 seconds because pnpm blocked build scripts for Clerk and two esbuild versions, so we never reached its build or tests.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for a drop-in starter: the README says this is not a starter project, and authentication is described as partial.

reviews.name: docs
reviews.verdict: Our Ink Docs build completed in 57 seconds after a 91-second install, but the measured checkout had no test target or Dockerfile, and the current repository declares no license.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for a reusable documentation starter with clear reuse rights: on September 15, 2026, GitHub detected no license, and the repository root had no license file.

reviews.name: remix
reviews.verdict: Our Remix 3 run installed 575 packages in 30 seconds and built in 31 seconds, but tests failed after 17 seconds because Playwright browser executables were absent.
reviews.skip_if: Existing Remix v1 or v2 teams seeking the supported continuation of that React framework: the maintainers moved that path into React Router 7.

reviews.name: fasthttp
reviews.verdict: Start with `net/http`, as fasthttp's own README recommends for most cases.
reviews.skip_if: Teams without a measured reason to replace `net/http`.

reviews.name: editor
reviews.verdict: Try Pascal Editor with a disposable building project if local editing and MCP access match your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a passing repository test command before evaluation: our recorded test command exited 1.

reviews.name: Graphite
reviews.verdict: Our Graphite dependency step installed 559 packages in 46 seconds, but both build and tests exceeded 900 seconds while Rust was still compiling.
reviews.skip_if: Production studios that need a stable document format or a 1.0 support promise: both remain roadmap items.

reviews.name: kumo
reviews.verdict: Kumo merits a consumer evaluation when Cloudflare's component system fits your React product.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a verified clean contributor baseline from this recorded checkout.

reviews.name: stremio-web
reviews.verdict: Stremio Web fits readers who want Stremio's addon experience in a browser or want to contribute to its interface.
reviews.skip_if: People expecting this UI repository to provide a complete media server by itself.

reviews.name: workout-guide
reviews.verdict: Our checkout built in 11 seconds and all five Vitest tests passed, so Workout Guide is a credible starting point for adding static exercise art without inventing a catalog.
reviews.skip_if: Products that need coaching, rep counting, timers, workout planning, or user progress: the project supplies exercise metadata and images, not a training engine.

reviews.name: edit
reviews.verdict: Use FMHY when you want a maintained map of free online resources and accept that many destinations are third-party sites requiring your own judgment.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors adding paid or trial-only services, coding libraries, Linux distributions, or multiplayer cheats: the contribution guide explicitly rejects those categories or directs readers elsewhere.

reviews.name: hugo
reviews.verdict: Hugo is a reasonable candidate for a static publication or documentation site when its templates, content model, and asset tooling fit the team.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting Hugo alone to supply request-time authentication, per-user responses, or application business logic.

reviews.name: router
reviews.verdict: Keep TanStack Router unless an application profile gives you a concrete reason to trial Speedy Router.
reviews.skip_if: Applications that require React 18 or documented Node 22 support.

reviews.name: topcoat
reviews.verdict: Our Topcoat run built in 241 seconds and all 239 tests passed in 151 seconds, giving this experimental framework a better code signal than its age suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams requiring API stability: the README calls Topcoat early-stage and experimental and says to expect breaking changes.

reviews.name: Viscose-carousel
reviews.verdict: Choose Viscose Carousel if its shader technique is worth the remaining application work.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing shareable project URLs and browser history behavior without implementing routing.

reviews.name: web-check
reviews.verdict: Web-Check is worth evaluating when you need several website investigations in one dashboard and can supply the services and system packages behind your chosen checks.
reviews.skip_if: Operators needing a fully offline investigation workflow: some checks require external APIs.

reviews.name: Infographic
reviews.verdict: Our AntV Infographic run built in 31 seconds and passed its 83-second test step, but installation took 207 seconds, used 986 MB, and exposed 4 high-severity advisories.
reviews.skip_if: Teams with a strict dependency-advisory gate: our install reported 7 known vulnerabilities, including 4 high-severity findings.

reviews.name: alphaprotein-novo
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox installed AlphaProtein Novo in 301 seconds and recorded 6,411 MB on disk, so even this small source checkout brings a substantial environment.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial organizations expecting access merely because an individual project is non-commercial: the generator terms restrict organizational eligibility.

reviews.name: AgentGarten
reviews.verdict: AgentGarten installed in 50 seconds and built in 1 second in our sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing the demonstrated worlds and agent practice loop as a complete runnable package.

reviews.name: VisionHOPE
reviews.verdict: Our VisionHOPE install succeeded in 41 seconds and occupied 5,419 MB, making this a substantial research environment for a small source checkout.
reviews.skip_if: Streaming applications expecting SRNL to remember previous forward calls: the public interface starts a new sequence each time.

reviews.name: nextai-translator
reviews.verdict: NextAI Translator merits a limited trial for readers who want provider-backed translation and rewriting in one interface.
reviews.skip_if: Users expecting to start without provider setup: the README's preparation section requires an API key.

reviews.name: annotated_deep_learning_paper_implementations
reviews.verdict: Our labml.ai installation occupied 5,379 MB and built successfully, but its test command ended with an optimizer timeout and a separate error.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a passing repository test run before adoption: our recorded command failed with an optimizer timeout and a separate collection/setup error.

reviews.name: KiroCrew
reviews.verdict: Kiro Crew completed dependency installation in 36 seconds and the build-labelled step in 50 seconds, but tests timed out after 900 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Operators expecting self-hosting to disable outbound telemetry by default: the README documents enabled usage heartbeats and official-app receipts, with opt-out controls.

reviews.name: openbot
reviews.verdict: OpenBot's repository checks passed, but its desktop workflows remain untested here.
reviews.skip_if: Users who require confirmation before each agent action.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: Higgsfield AI Skills requires an authenticated Higgsfield CLI workflow, and our lab did not execute it.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring offline inference: the documented generation flow submits jobs through an authenticated Higgsfield CLI.

reviews.name: Beav
reviews.verdict: Our Beav run completed the npm step in 4 seconds but found no build or test target, leaving the desktop application unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need the source for the current desktop release: the repository identifies the public baseline as 2.5.0 and says later release notes do not publish corresponding source.

reviews.name: V3R1T4S
reviews.verdict: Use V3R1T4S for supervised research where you can inspect the object, checker and success criterion.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need outside expert review before relying on a finding.

reviews.name: hypoarena
reviews.verdict: Our Hypoarena run installed 48 packages into 176 MB and passed its build and 47-second test step, making the offline workbench practical to try.
reviews.skip_if: Scientists seeking answers from real papers out of the box: the default commands use synthetic corpora and scripted or replayed agents.

reviews.name: ollaya
reviews.verdict: Our Ollaya run installed 328 packages in 10 seconds, then failed to build after 150 seconds with undefined C++ symbols, so a fresh Debian source checkout needs more work before adoption.
reviews.skip_if: Developers needing a working source build in a fresh Debian container: our build and test commands both stopped at linking.

reviews.name: awesome-opus5-5-videos
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run Awesome Opus 5.5 Videos because the collection had no supported ecosystem or Dockerfile, so it offers no measured execution result.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a runnable video pipeline: this is a prompt and reference collection, and our harness found no supported ecosystem.

reviews.name: Fuxi
reviews.verdict: We did not run FuXi at commit f70cb3a because our harness lacked a supported ecosystem and the checkout had no Dockerfile, so its runtime remains unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Developers requiring an open-source, forkable agent: the README and LICENSE say the implementation is proprietary and unpublished.

reviews.name: jarvis
reviews.verdict: Our Jarvis run used 7,014 MB after installation and ended with 23 failed tests, 177 collection/setup errors, and 121 known vulnerabilities reported by pip-audit.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial product teams expecting unrestricted reuse: the license requires a separate commercial license.

reviews.name: onetake
reviews.verdict: Try onetake for a noncommercial film experiment if you want to work with its continuity method and can review the resulting composition yourself.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial teams relying on the public edition's license: the README prohibits commercial use and directs those users to onetake Pro.

reviews.name: omarchy-meeting-recorder
reviews.verdict: Our Omarchy Meeting Recorder build failed after 23 seconds because GTK 4.8.3 did not satisfy its GTK 4.12 minimum, so source setup needs a compatible desktop before you can judge the recorder.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting an older GTK desktop to compile it unchanged: our GTK 4.8.3 failed the required GTK 4.12 check.

reviews.name: AionUi
reviews.verdict: Our AionUi run passed 4,980 tests but failed its build after 81 seconds while preparing bundled AionCore resources, so we cannot recommend this commit as ready for source packaging.
reviews.skip_if: Windows users who need Antigravity with approval prompts: open issue 4317 reports failed tool hooks in v2.2.2, with Full Auto bypassing approval as the workaround.

reviews.name: bridgeclip
reviews.verdict: Our BridgeClip build passed in 11 seconds, but its test suite ended with 226 passes and 3 failures, so the source is a candidate for an attended trial rather than unattended publishing.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose recordings must stay entirely offline: audio and transcripts go to OpenRouter, and some visual paths send sampled frames.

reviews.name: mini-AGI
reviews.verdict: Our mini-AGI run installed 35 packages in 15 seconds and built in 4 seconds, but supplied no test result because the repository had no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing a dependable local assistant now: the README calls the model toy-level and says final weights are unavailable.

reviews.name: OpenIntelligentUI
reviews.verdict: Our OpenIntelligentUI run installed 1,196 packages into 1,276 MB, then passed its build and all 4 Vitest tests, making the repository a workable starting point for interactive answers.
reviews.skip_if: People requiring offline or credential-free chat: the browser flow requires both OpenAI and Jev keys and makes billed provider requests.

reviews.name: jev-chat-windows
reviews.verdict: Our JevChat-Windows run installed 35 packages in 28 seconds and built successfully, but skipped tests because no target was available.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users expecting a fully English interface and manual: the README is Chinese and interface choices are Chinese or Korean.

reviews.name: jev-chat-jarvis
reviews.verdict: We did not run Jev because our harness lacked Kotlin support and the repo had no Dockerfile, so we cannot endorse its Android execution or reply accuracy.
reviews.skip_if: WhatsApp Business users or people whose conversations happen in groups: the global README excludes both.

reviews.name: cindy
reviews.verdict: Our Cindy install used 4,102 MB, then the build failed because Electron Forge couldn't find dpkg and fakeroot, so source adoption needs packaging preparation.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing the complete backend in the same open repository: the README says this checkout contains only clients and shared packages.

reviews.name: Hy-MT2
reviews.verdict: Our Hy-MT2 run prepared IFMTBench with 37 packages and 38 MB, built in 1 second, and supplied no translation-quality result.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting a ready translation API from cloning this repository: deployment requires separate model weights and an inference runtime.

reviews.name: jev-align
reviews.verdict: Our jev-align run installed 160 packages into 866 MB, passed its build and tests, and still returned 2 known vulnerabilities, so a trial is justified but a blind rollout is not.
reviews.skip_if: High-stakes evaluation teams until they examine issue #3: it reports a correct all-negative held-out round displayed as F1 0.000.

reviews.name: awesome-jev-tools
reviews.verdict: The 23 published category counts add up to 1,192 records, making awesome-jev-tools broad enough for discovery but far too broad to substitute for evaluation.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking runnable software: this repository is a Markdown index with no supported executable ecosystem or Dockerfile.

reviews.name: agency-agents-app
reviews.verdict: Agency Agents App is worth evaluating if you want a desktop interface for installing and tracking persona files across coding tools.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking an agent runtime or orchestration system.

reviews.name: nimble
reviews.verdict: Our Nimble run installed 35 packages and built successfully, but its 143-test suite ended with 2 failures and 16 collection/setup errors, so this is a promising research recipe with unfinished setup edges.
reviews.skip_if: CPU-only Linux deployments: the README requires Apple Silicon on macOS or an NVIDIA GPU with BF16 support for local inference.

reviews.name: localjev
reviews.verdict: Our LocalJev run installed 9 packages in 12 seconds and passed all 19 tests, but it did not exercise the required model server or prove that its generated probabilities are calibrated.
reviews.skip_if: Systems that require probabilities read directly from model logits: the README says LocalJev's values are generated by the model and are not mathematically equivalent to OpenJev's structured read.

reviews.name: ZeroScript-Free
reviews.verdict: Our ZeroScript-Free run installed 35 packages in 7 seconds and built in 1, but it had no test target, so the code is easy to unpack and hard to verify automatically.
reviews.skip_if: Linux or Firefox users: the README supports Windows or macOS with Edge or Chrome, while Linux and Firefox support remain open requests.

reviews.name: jevlike
reviews.verdict: Our Jevlike run installed 64 packages and occupied 5,379 MB, then passed its single test in 16 seconds, so the model is easy to inspect but lightly proved.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a drop-in copy of TypeSafe's Jev: the README calls this an independent starter and says Jev's design is private.

reviews.name: ARTEX
reviews.verdict: Our ARTEX run built in 66 seconds, but its 99-second test step ended with 28 passing and 3 failing tests out of 31.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone conducting a real penetration test, including an authorized test of an owned system: the README expressly limits ARTEX to learning, source research, and isolated local validation, and forbids tests against any online or networked system.

reviews.name: reelbench-skills
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run commit 1b51af8 because the repository fell outside the supported runner and has no Dockerfile, so its scripts and advertised gates remain unverified by us.
reviews.skip_if: Editors who need automatic transcription, face recognition, or object detection: video-shots explicitly excludes all three.

reviews.name: flybook
reviews.verdict: Our run passed 41 tests and built in 5 seconds, but pip-audit reported 20 known vulnerabilities and the project has not demonstrated profitable learning.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a proven trading bot: the model documentation says no profitable learning or strategy improvement has been demonstrated.

reviews.name: crypto-rag
reviews.verdict: Our Crypto RAG run installed 35 packages in 15 seconds and passed its 5-second build, but it exposed no automated test target for retrieval, routing, or market calculations.
reviews.skip_if: Traders placing orders from the reported spread: the comparison mixes raw USDT and USD quotes without an explicit currency conversion.

reviews.name: Choruz
reviews.verdict: Our Choruz run installed 559 packages and used 954 MB, yet exposed no supported build or test target to our harness, so adopting it means accepting a large developer-preview system without our usual verification step.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing a stable production contract today: the README labels Choruz a developer preview and warns that interfaces, configuration, and data formats may change incompatibly.

reviews.name: lieflat-gongwen
reviews.verdict: Our Lieflat Gongwen run installed 35 packages in 28 seconds and built in 5 seconds, but there was no test target to check its writing workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial writing services or paid software products: the PolyForm Noncommercial license bars commercial use without a separate agreement.

reviews.name: UniMate
reviews.verdict: Our UniMate run installed 35 packages in 25 seconds and built in 7 seconds, but it exposed no test target and did not exercise checkpoint inference.
reviews.skip_if: Mac or Apple Silicon users: the maintainer says current inference supports NVIDIA CUDA only.

reviews.name: cyber-resume-reviewer-skill
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox produced no install, build, or test result for commit 263acc3 because the runner found no supported executable ecosystem and the repo has no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Recruiters building candidate ranking or interview prediction software: the skill expressly refuses both jobs.

reviews.name: holo-card
reviews.verdict: Our optional-API run installed 7 packages in 7 seconds and passed its tests in 14 seconds, but those tests use a mock provider and cannot judge the generated card.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a one-click filter: the README requires separate layer generation, matte repair, alignment checks, and visual inspection.

reviews.name: Awesome-OKF
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 35 packages in 16 seconds and passed all 9 tests, but the advertised PyPI command still fails because Awesome-OKF has not been published there.
reviews.skip_if: Users following the README's `pipx install awesome-okf` command: open issue 14 says the package has never been published to PyPI, so install from Git is required.

reviews.name: dream-loop
reviews.verdict: Our Dream Loop run installed 35 packages in 23 seconds and built in 10 seconds, but there was no test target and we did not exercise its visual loop, so the clean setup says nothing about output fidelity.
reviews.skip_if: Developers whose agent lacks image generation or vision: the skill requires both and tells the agent to stop when no target image can be supplied.

reviews.name: holo-card-studio
reviews.verdict: Use Holo Card Studio for a supervised trial when editable Blender output and a browser viewer fit your task.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring demonstrated unattended card generation from this review Users expecting our sandbox results to establish Blender-version or touch-device compatibility Print production teams seeking evidence of manufacturing-ready output; the supplied documentation describes digital scenes, images, and a viewer

reviews.name: novoweave
reviews.verdict: Our NovoWeave run installed 51 packages in 16 seconds and passed all 8 tests, proving that the scaffold is easy to inspect, not that it can design a protein.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs generated structures or sequences: the README says there are no weights, datasets, checkpoints, tensor kernels, loss functions, or samplers.

reviews.name: rizzo-pii
reviews.verdict: Our Rizzo PII install consumed 5,741 MB, and pytest crashed before collecting a single test, so the clean audit and 1-second build do not establish a safe document pipeline.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that need certified coverage outside Italian: the README says the other seven trained languages are not validated.

reviews.name: awesome-ai-agent-platforms
reviews.verdict: Our commit 1b2dff2 checkout installed 35 packages in 12 seconds and built in 2 seconds, but it had no test target for the 49 entries.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers seeking a ranked winner or performance comparison: the selection policy says inclusion is not an endorsement and does not use star counts, funding, or company size.

reviews.name: image-story-video-wizard
reviews.verdict: Our Image Story Video Wizard run passed all 9 tests in 7 seconds, but those checks cover the workflow package rather than TTS, image generation, or a final render.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a one-command video generator: the skill pauses for user decisions and depends on separately available writing, TTS, image, and rendering tools.

reviews.name: aipass-bridge
reviews.verdict: Our aipass-bridge run installed 629 packages, passed all 148 tests, and reported 0 known vulnerabilities, but the useful runtime still depends on a logged-in browser and an unauthenticated local port.
reviews.skip_if: Cursor, Cline, Continue, or similar agent users: the README says system prompts and earlier messages are dropped, so those clients lose their tools and transcript.

reviews.name: image-prompt-reverse
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox found no supported runtime and no Dockerfile at commit 4dead0a, so Image Prompt Reverse is a readable Codex instruction pack rather than software we could execute.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for a standalone image-analysis program or API: the repository contains Codex instructions, reference Markdown, and interface metadata, with no supported runtime or Dockerfile.

reviews.name: freemocap
reviews.verdict: Our FreeMoCap build took 1 second, but 9 of 44 tests never collected because `libGL.so.1` was missing, and pip-audit found 4 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Researchers who need dependable physical scale today: the v2.0.0-alpha.25 notes warn that skeleton reconstructions may be off by roughly 10%.

reviews.name: langextract
reviews.verdict: Consider LangExtract when reviewers need to trace extracted phrases back to a document.
reviews.skip_if: Workflows that require correct fields without validation or human review.

reviews.name: openrig
reviews.verdict: Our OpenRig run installed 492 packages, found 21 known vulnerabilities, and ended with 4 failed tests out of 201 after a successful 57-second build.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone wanting a small wrapper around one coding agent: our install pulled 492 packages and used 255 MB before any provider tooling.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run pashov/skills because the JavaScript repository had no supported execution ecosystem and no Dockerfile, so there is no build or test result to support a reliability claim.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a deterministic scanner with a conventional test binary: this repository is primarily agent instructions, scripts, and templates.

reviews.name: starnet
reviews.verdict: Our StarNet checkout occupied 3,365 MB, installed another 1,598 MB, and still ended its test command with exit code 1, so source adoption demands more patience than the playful station suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Linux desktop users: the install guide says Linux artifacts are internal and the public release train supports only Windows and macOS.

reviews.name: hexstellar
reviews.verdict: Our HexStellar install took 22 seconds and the build passed in 1 second, but the checkout had no test target for the 119-file client.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking an open-source solver they can inspect or modify: the license is proprietary, and the repository says the engine is sealed and remote.

reviews.name: autoclip
reviews.verdict: Our AutoClip run installed only 4 root npm packages in 3 seconds, while the full 71,462-line product exposed no root build or test target to our harness, so the lab result is far too narrow to call the pipeline proven.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting our lab result to validate the full product: it covered the root npm package, not Python, the nested frontend, Rust, FFmpeg, Redis, Celery, or a real video.

reviews.name: Portable-Local-Studio
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox installed 30 packages in 4 seconds and built the frontend in 1 second, but the repository had no test target to exercise its four AI workspaces.

reviews.name: GLiNER2

reviews.verdict: Use andrej-karpathy-skills if your main complaint is that Claude Code guesses too much, edits too broadly, or turns small jobs into large designs.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need measured proof that the rules improve coding outcomes: the tested commit contains examples, while a benchmark and runner remain in an open pull request.

reviews.name: opa
reviews.verdict: Evaluate OPA when moving shared policy rules out of services solves a concrete maintenance problem and your team will own enforcement.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting an authorization decision to enforce itself: the application still has to act on OPA's answer.

reviews.name: no-mistakes
reviews.verdict: No Mistakes merits a supervised trial for developers who want agent review integrated with their push workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a verified enforcement boundary: our test command failed, and the complete agent-to-PR workflow was not tested.

reviews.name: zizmor
reviews.verdict: zizmor is worth evaluating for maintainers who want static security review of CI/CD configuration.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking demonstrated coverage of CI formats beyond the inputs documented here.

reviews.name: anti-slop
reviews.verdict: Trial anti-slop when you want to own and adjust a stricter Oxlint policy.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring an official npm package and ordinary package-manager updates.

reviews.name: PLFM_RADAR
reviews.verdict: Study AERIS-10 if your team can review the boards and own hardware bring-up.
reviews.skip_if: Builders expecting a complete assembly recipe: the README says a standalone assembly guide is not currently tracked.

reviews.name: ESP32-Cheap-Yellow-Display
reviews.verdict: Use ESP32-Cheap-Yellow-Display for board-specific setup guidance after checking the ESP32-2432S028 marking.
reviews.skip_if: Owners assuming every board sold as a Cheap Yellow Display uses the same pins.

reviews.name: RustPython
reviews.verdict: Evaluate RustPython when an interpreter implemented in Rust solves a specific embedding or WebAssembly requirement.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring demonstrated production readiness: the README says RustPython is not totally production-ready.

reviews.name: syft
reviews.verdict: Syft is worth evaluating when you need SBOM generation across container images and filesystems, several output formats, or a Go library.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting Syft's inventory command alone to report known vulnerabilities.

reviews.name: typescript-go
reviews.verdict: Start new TypeScript work in microsoft/TypeScript.
reviews.skip_if: New contributors looking for the project's development venue: follow the redirect to microsoft/TypeScript.

reviews.name: devenv
reviews.verdict: devenv is a reasonable candidate for teams that want tools, services and tasks under shared Nix configuration.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that cannot install Nix on developer machines.

reviews.name: sourcebot
reviews.verdict: Sourcebot v6.0.0 requires deployment activation and removes anonymous access, while current development has moved to a private repository.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring inspectable current application source: the maintainer moved development into a private repository starting with v6.

reviews.name: writer-computer
reviews.verdict: Our Writer checkout installed 683 packages in 10 seconds and occupied 522 MB, yet its root provided no build or test target that the lab could run.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users seeking a released app: v0.5.0 ships an Apple Silicon DMG and macOS app archive, while open issues request Windows 11 and Linux releases Users who need mobile sync, collaboration, publishing, or a hosted account: the README…

reviews.name: Dopamine
reviews.verdict: Dopamine is the leading option to try when its exact hardware and iOS matrix matches your device and you want a modern rootless jailbreak.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone outside the published chip and iOS combinations: the README says version-support issues will be deleted without a response, so unsupported devices are not an experimental target.

reviews.name: yq
reviews.verdict: Consider Mike Farah's yq for targeted YAML queries, updates and conversions when jq-like syntax fits your scripts and output diffs are acceptable.
reviews.skip_if: Scripts requiring complete jq compatibility.

reviews.name: osv-scanner
reviews.verdict: OSV-Scanner is worth evaluating for dependency vulnerability checks when your actual inputs match its documented extractors.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking evidence that the scanner detects arbitrary application flaws: this review evaluates dependency vulnerability scanning.

reviews.name: fff
reviews.verdict: FFF is worth evaluating when an editor or agent repeatedly searches the same repository and can reuse a resident index.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a verified search-speed or memory benchmark: our recorded run measured neither.

reviews.name: ucp
reviews.verdict: Evaluate UCP when independently operated commerce systems need a shared contract.
reviews.skip_if: Merchants expecting this checkout to provide a running commerce backend, dashboard or storefront.

reviews.name: DevOps-Interview-Guide
reviews.verdict: Use DevOps-Interview-Guide to rehearse explanations after you have learned the underlying subjects.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners who need a course with explanations and worked answers: the two inspected interview files contain questions without worked solutions.

reviews.name: Lighthouse
reviews.verdict: Lighthouse is worth considering if you own a supported Banjo-Kazooie ROM and want its documented desktop settings or mod features.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot supply a supported game ROM: the release does not include the game's copyrighted assets.

reviews.name: caddy
reviews.verdict: Caddy is worth evaluating when automatic certificate management is a main reason for choosing a web server or reverse proxy.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require adding plugins to an unchanged executable: Caddy's documented custom-module build compiles imports into the binary.

reviews.name: deepseek-harness-linux
reviews.verdict: Use deepseek-harness-linux if you want a community Linux desktop and can troubleshoot packaging and plugins.
reviews.skip_if: Workflows requiring desktop DOCX, XLSX or PPTX conversion to PDF, which the README says is unavailable.

reviews.name: uzu
reviews.verdict: Shortlist uzu for an Apple app evaluation if its documented device support and model workflow fit the project.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring documented support beyond Apple Silicon on iOS and macOS: the supplied FAQ does not establish that support.

reviews.name: scion
reviews.verdict: Our Scion build succeeded in 395 seconds, but its test step ended with 9 failures out of 105 results, so commit 18d1bb3 needs investigation before unattended use.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who wants agent commands without a background service: the README requires a Hub even on a single-user workstation.

reviews.name: iCode
reviews.verdict: Our iCode install took 12 seconds and its build passed, but pytest stopped after 2 seconds because it rejected -n.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring stable configuration contracts: the README warns that interfaces, file formats and defaults change between releases.

reviews.name: Strata
reviews.verdict: Our Strata run installed 45 packages in 11 seconds, but pytest stopped with 5 collection/setup errors because llama.cpp's gguf-py was missing.
reviews.skip_if: PCs below the documented 12 GB VRAM and 32 GB RAM baseline: model fit depends on both kinds of memory.

reviews.name: magpie
reviews.verdict: Our Magpie build succeeded in 49 seconds, but its test step reported 63 failures out of 109 results, so a successful build is insufficient evidence for adopting this gateway unattended.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone happy with one agent on its native subscription: the README says that use case does not need Magpie.

reviews.name: billion-context
reviews.verdict: Our billion-context run built in 26 seconds, but its tests timed out at 900 seconds and npm audit reported 22 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Claude Desktop Code-tab users: the README says its URL override bypasses the native proxy while native automatic compaction can remain disabled.

reviews.name: CodeAF
reviews.verdict: Our CodeAF build passed in 134 seconds, but its tests timed out at 900 seconds with 168 passes and 4 recorded failures, so the source setup is usable without being cleared by a complete green suite.
reviews.skip_if: Operators requiring a green complete source suite before adoption: our tests timed out after 900 seconds with 4 recorded failures.

reviews.name: simple-jev
reviews.verdict: Our Simple Jev environment occupied 5,478 MB and its only collected test errored on a missing `pydantic` module, so self-hosting is a serious ML setup rather than a simple classifier install.
reviews.skip_if: Small containers or casual local trials: our RFDT-scoped environment used 5,478 MB after 82 packages.

reviews.name: OptMem
reviews.verdict: Our OptMem run installed 38 packages for the explainer in 4 seconds but found no build or test target, so it did not verify the Python memory tool that users actually depend on.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that need an explicit software license: the repository has no license file, GitHub reports none, and issue 8 asks for one.

reviews.name: SemIf-OpenJev
reviews.verdict: Our SemIf run passed 67 tests in 11 seconds, but its 83-package environment occupied 7,074 MB and pip-audit found 5 known vulnerabilities, so the clean test result is only the start of adoption.
reviews.skip_if: Business rules that must always be deterministic: SemIf returns model probabilities, and the README says they are conditional on the supplied options.

reviews.name: deepseek-recipe
reviews.verdict: Our DeepSeek Recipe run downloaded 306 packages, then both build and tests stopped because OpenCV was not installed or discoverable.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a ready DeepSeek server: the README says model inference, HTTP transport, and tool execution are external.

reviews.name: claude-style-patch
reviews.verdict: Commit b62aa1b gave our lab no executable path to test, so Claude Style Patch is best judged as a three-file editorial policy, not software.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking an executable formatter or pass/fail linter: the repository contains prose instructions, not a checker.

reviews.name: agent-memory
reviews.verdict: Our run installed Agent Memory in 27 seconds and built it in 10 seconds, then pytest exited 4 because `agent_memory` could not be imported.
reviews.skip_if: Release pipelines that require a green clean-container suite: our pytest step exited 4 because `agent_memory` could not be imported from `tests/conftest.py`.

reviews.name: train-llm-from-scratch
reviews.verdict: Train LLM From Scratch is worth considering for learning how a shared model backbone supports different training objectives.
reviews.skip_if: Readers expecting a verified recipe for training a competitive commercial assistant: our recorded run does not establish model quality or large-scale training performance.

reviews.name: OpenContext
reviews.verdict: Our OpenContext install pulled 1,041 packages and 821 MB, while npm audit reported 37 known vulnerabilities including 1 critical, so the dependency tree needs review before this belongs on a sensitive workstation.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive workstations that cannot accept the measured dependency state: npm audit reported 37 known vulnerabilities, including 1 critical and 22 high.

reviews.name: ChatGPT
reviews.verdict: Our lencx/ChatGPT source install stopped after 9 seconds because pnpm reported an ignored esbuild build script, leaving the desktop app unevaluated.
reviews.skip_if: Teams choosing a new supported daily client: the README points to Noi, while the last source push was August 29, 2024.

reviews.name: chat-on-steroids
reviews.verdict: Try Chat On Steroids when keeping browser ChatGPT as your working interface is worth configuring and supervising its local access.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require publisher-signed Windows or macOS packages: the supplied README describes unsigned beta builds, with macOS also unnotarized.

reviews.name: agentic-api
reviews.verdict: Our Agentic API run installed 36 Python packages and built in 6 seconds, but pytest ended with 2 failures and 1 collection or setup error after 109 tests passed.
reviews.skip_if: Zero-data-retention deployments using WebSockets until issue 238 is resolved: it reports that `store: false` state remains retrievable across new connections.

reviews.name: a2ui
reviews.verdict: A2UI is worth a bounded evaluation when client-owned components and a shared agent UI format solve your integration problem.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a frozen specification: upstream calls A2UI an early public preview and says to expect changes.

reviews.name: open-knowledge
reviews.verdict: Try a copied folder if OpenKnowledge's documented visual editing and agent access match your work.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors who need a checkout already validated to build in our recorded environment.

reviews.name: patent-disclosure-skill
reviews.verdict: Our run passed 179 of 182 collected tests, but 2 tests failed and 1 collection or setup error remained, so Patent Disclosure Skill should be treated as a review-heavy drafting aid.
reviews.skip_if: English-only teams: the working instructions and detailed installation material are primarily Chinese, with no equivalent full English guide.

reviews.name: oh-my-hermes
reviews.verdict: Evaluate OMH for a specific workflow gap in an existing Hermes installation.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a standalone replacement for Hermes Agent.

reviews.name: agentgateway
reviews.verdict: Agentgateway merits a deployment trial when shared controls for LLM, MCP, and A2A traffic solve an existing platform problem.
reviews.skip_if: A single application with one provider and no shared policy requirement, unless the additional proxy has a clear operational purpose.

reviews.name: opencode-mem
reviews.verdict: OpenCode Memory is worth a controlled evaluation if you want persistent context inside OpenCode and can accept its provider and platform requirements.
reviews.skip_if: Intel Mac users: the README says local persistence lacks a required darwin/x64 native binding.

reviews.name: opik
reviews.verdict: Opik is a trial candidate for teams that need tracing and dataset evaluation together.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who only need ordinary local application logs and have no use for a separate tracing and evaluation platform.

reviews.name: Megatron-LM
reviews.verdict: Megatron-LM is worth evaluating when NVIDIA GPU training and explicit control over parallelism fit your requirements.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking evidence of training throughput, convergence or multi-node correctness from our sandbox: we did not test those workloads.

reviews.name: deepagents
reviews.verdict: Our Deep Agents run installed in 27 seconds and built in 4 seconds, but its libs/acp test command exited 3 before any tests passed or failed.
reviews.skip_if: Applications needing a custom workflow graph rather than the bundled agent loop: the README directs those users to LangGraph.

reviews.name: mcp-toolbox
reviews.verdict: MCP Toolbox for Databases is worth evaluating when several agents or applications need shared, predefined database operations.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require verified database compatibility or production security results before evaluation: our recorded run establishes neither.

reviews.name: book-to-skill
reviews.verdict: Use book-to-skill as an interesting local workflow, not yet as trusted knowledge infrastructure.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a polished hosted app with account sync and support People working mainly with scanned PDFs, because OCR must happen first Teams that need verbatim, citation-grade retrieval from source pages Users unwilling to install format-specific tools or inspect generated…

reviews.name: dsh-routing-suite
reviews.verdict: dsh-routing-suite merits a controlled trial for existing DSH users who need its plugin, reasoning or task-protocol controls.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking verified improvements in task completion, routing accuracy or API spending: our sandbox did not measure those outcomes.

reviews.name: semantic-router
reviews.verdict: Evaluate vLLM Semantic Router for explicit model-selection policy across existing backends, with a narrow deployment trial before broader adoption.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting the Router to provision generation backends: those endpoints must be supplied separately.

reviews.name: slime
reviews.verdict: Evaluate slime if you want direct Megatron and SGLang integration with custom rollout and reward workflows.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a laptop-only introduction to reinforcement learning: the documented environment starts with a GPU host and a prepared software stack.

reviews.name: Kun
reviews.verdict: Kun is worth a bounded noncommercial evaluation when sharing desktop and terminal context matters to your work.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial users without separate written permission from the author.

reviews.name: embabel-agent
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Embabel Agent if reusable typed actions and runtime planning solve a concrete problem in your Spring application.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking evidence here that the JVM build or test suite passed: our attached run contains neither.

reviews.name: ds4
reviews.verdict: Evaluate DwarfStar for a specific supported model on its intended hardware, accepting the documented beta status.
reviews.skip_if: Users expecting arbitrary GGUF compatibility.

reviews.name: aurelio-finance
reviews.verdict: Technical households willing to maintain manual snapshots, run the source installation and keep database backups can start with the documented invented-household demo.
reviews.skip_if: People who require automatic bank or broker synchronization.

reviews.name: run-ai
reviews.verdict: Our Run:ai MCP server run passed all 20 recorded Go tests, but did not deploy the Kubernetes GPU platform.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a standalone GPU runtime: Run:ai requires Kubernetes and adds control-plane and cluster services.

reviews.name: woodpecker
reviews.verdict: Shortlist Woodpecker if your team is prepared to operate forge authentication, a server, agents and database recovery.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring user accounts independent of their Git host: the documented authentication uses forge accounts through OAuth2.

reviews.name: localthings
reviews.verdict: LocalThings is worth a model-specific trial for Home Assistant owners seeking local Samsung commands who can handle the documented authentication limits.
reviews.skip_if: Owners whose appliance rejects the automatic certificate and who cannot obtain the required pre-shared key.

reviews.name: kubevirt
reviews.verdict: Evaluate KubeVirt when your team already operates Kubernetes and needs VM lifecycle management through its API.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a standalone virtualization appliance rather than an add-on to an existing Kubernetes cluster.

reviews.name: linkwarden
reviews.verdict: Linkwarden's Yarn install failed after 121 seconds in our sandbox, with browser setup reporting a root-authentication failure.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a local-only mobile bookmark app: the official app needs an account on a hosted or self-hosted Linkwarden instance.

reviews.name: ha-mcp
reviews.verdict: HA MCP installed in 31 seconds and built in 11 seconds in our sandbox, but pytest stopped with 200 collection/setup errors before any test passed.
reviews.skip_if: Users who only need device control and home-state queries: Home Assistant's own MCP integration already documents those functions.

reviews.name: bloom
reviews.verdict: Our Bloom installation and build each succeeded in 27 seconds, but tests were skipped and native Windows taskbar behavior remains unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Users who only want desktop meters or a visualizer: Bloom also replaces the native taskbar, expanding the scope of the change.

reviews.name: edge-smart-doh
reviews.verdict: Our Edge Smart DoH run passed all 196 tests in 5 seconds and reported 0 known npm vulnerabilities, making it a credible candidate for a targeted DNS experiment.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a proxy or IP anonymity: the README says traffic still goes directly from the client to Cloudflare.

reviews.name: Arrmada
reviews.verdict: Our Arrmada run built in 1 second, but its Go suite failed after 457 seconds with 120 passing results and 6 failures, so I would trial it beside a working library before migrating.
reviews.skip_if: Operators expecting a fully passing fresh-container suite: our Go run ended with 6 failures.

reviews.name: invisible_dots
reviews.verdict: Our Dots run built in 36 seconds, but its suite ended with 2,205 passing tests, 1 failure and 9 skipped.
reviews.skip_if: Mac users: the guide explicitly excludes macOS hosts.

reviews.name: DiPlay
reviews.verdict: Our DiPlay run installed in 23 seconds, but both build and test commands failed after 11 seconds in the Gradle HTTPS fetch path.
reviews.skip_if: Owners requiring Apple certification or assured compatibility with future iOS updates: the README explicitly disclaims both and describes an extractable experimental identity.

reviews.name: papermono-shopping-list
reviews.verdict: Our PaperMono server run passed all 120 tests in 7 seconds after a 13-second install, making the software worth trying for an existing PaperMono owner.
reviews.skip_if: Households expecting a finished appliance: the README calls this a personal project and says only the PaperMono C153 has been tested.

reviews.name: slashdocs
reviews.verdict: Trial Slashdocs for reviewing agent-generated HTML when you can operate its supporting services and validate the full workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that cannot provide different hostnames for the application and uploaded document rendering.

reviews.name: streambert
reviews.verdict: Our StreamBert install took 17 seconds and used 441 MB, with 0 known vulnerabilities reported, but build, tests, and playback were not verified.
reviews.skip_if: Viewers expecting dependable playback from a stable catalog: issue 183 reports blank playback, and the maintainer reported Videasy shutting down in issue 180.

reviews.name: YesPlayMusic
reviews.verdict: Our YesPlayMusic install failed after 5 seconds because Yarn rejected Node 18.20.8 against the declared Node 14 or 16 range.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking an independent server for their own music library: the documented web deployment depends on the NetEase API service.

reviews.name: slot
reviews.verdict: Our Slot build succeeded in 96 seconds, but tests failed after 34 seconds while compiling a recording example that imports a macOS-only graphics surface.
reviews.skip_if: Players wanting other consoles: the README limits support to GB, GBC, and GBA.

reviews.name: lxserver
reviews.verdict: Choose lxserver for an LX Music workflow that benefits from browser playback and server library management, provided you can configure access and verify your chosen sources.
reviews.skip_if: People expecting playlist sync to copy their audio collection onto every device.

reviews.name: VERT
reviews.verdict: Our VERT run installed 389 packages and occupied 965 MB, then failed its build after 18 seconds, leaving source deployment unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Air-gapped deployments expecting the external-request switch to remove every network dependency: the FAQ retains an FFmpeg fetch from cdn.jsdelivr.net.

reviews.name: esp32-c3-adblock
reviews.verdict: ESP32-C3 Adblock fits a roughly 100,000-entry default DNS list onto a 4 MB board without PSRAM, but its administration stays on plain HTTP.
reviews.skip_if: Networks that require encrypted administration: the README says the dashboard uses plain HTTP on port 80, so Basic Auth credentials can be read by someone already sniffing the LAN.

reviews.name: UFI-TOOLS
reviews.verdict: Our UFI-TOOLS install stopped after 6 seconds at pnpm's build-script approval check, so we could not verify a working frontend from the measured checkout.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need English installation support: the README and long user manual are Chinese, and neither links an English guide.

reviews.name: lunel
reviews.verdict: Our Lunel run installed 62 packages in 28 seconds and all 45 tests passed, but the project has no visible CI workflow or tagged GitHub release, so it is promising code with a short public operating record.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone likely to leave first-login defaults unchanged: the quick start publishes `admin / admin` and tells you to replace it immediately.

reviews.name: printfilm
reviews.verdict: Our PrintFilm backend installed 102 packages and built in 34 seconds combined, then ended with 4 failed tests, 73 setup errors, and 40 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: English-only teams: the README, interface conventions, deployment notes, and product rules are written in Simplified Chinese with no English guide.

reviews.name: Spun
reviews.verdict: Our Spun helper run installed 42 packages in 18 seconds and built in 6 seconds, but pytest collected 0 tests and exited 5, so it does not establish that the C++ player works on our box.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial products or services: PolyForm Noncommercial restricts use outside its listed permissions, and no commercial edition is offered.

reviews.name: AgentENV
reviews.verdict: Our AgentENV run passed 1,810 of 1,852 tests, but the build timed out at 900 seconds and 42 tests failed, so this is promising infrastructure that still needs a hardware-matched evaluation before production.
reviews.skip_if: Developers on ordinary laptops or restricted containers: the server requires Linux kernel 6.8 or newer, `/dev/kvm`, and sudo or privileged Docker access.

reviews.name: PanWatch
reviews.verdict: Evaluate PanWatch for combined portfolio monitoring and AI research, with export and integration checks before reliance.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone requiring verified searchable PDF reports without deployment-specific checks: the stored run recorded two PDF text-extraction assertion failures whose cause remains unresolved.

reviews.name: OpenStock
reviews.verdict: Our OpenStock run passed 79 tests but failed its 18-second production build, while npm reported 71 known vulnerabilities, so this commit is better source material than a ready deployment.
reviews.skip_if: Investors who need an order-entry system: the README says OpenStock is not a brokerage.

reviews.name: celld
reviews.verdict: Our celld build took 445 seconds, and its 55-second `cargo test` run discovered 0 tests, so v0.5.0 asks operators to assess a young distributed-state system without executed test coverage from our run.
reviews.skip_if: Hosts running mutually untrusted customer code: the security guide says the alpha is unsafe for hostile multi-tenant use and trusts the application.

reviews.name: forem
reviews.verdict: Our Forem run built successfully in 6 seconds but finished with 44 failing Jest tests.
reviews.skip_if: Operators whose database service cannot provide pgvector 0.8.0 or higher: the supplied README makes the extension mandatory even when Gemini recommendations are disabled.

reviews.name: openfang
reviews.verdict: Our OpenFang build took 729 seconds, then all 5,398 cargo tests passed in 600 seconds, which makes the code worth evaluating but does not settle its open security and cost-control reports.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a settled production release and a current roadmap: OpenFang is pre-1.0, v0.6.9 was released on May 12, 2026, and an open status request has no maintainer response.

reviews.name: checkcle
reviews.verdict: CheckCle built in 14 seconds in our sandbox, but tests were skipped and npm audit reported 39 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a passing automated test result from our evaluation: the measured application had no test script or target, so tests were skipped.

reviews.name: gotohp
reviews.verdict: gotohp installed in 42 seconds and built in 1 second in our sandbox, but its test command failed while the log reported missing webkitgtk-6.0.
reviews.skip_if: Managed-account users whose policy forbids copying sign-in cookies or Android credentials: every documented account route requires extracting one of those secrets.

reviews.name: Mailspring
reviews.verdict: Our Mailspring install ran for 380 seconds before `better-sqlite3` 12.11.1 failed in node-gyp, leaving no build or test result.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors expecting the README's two-command source setup to be dependable: our install failed after 380 seconds in the native `better-sqlite3` build.

reviews.name: danmu_api
reviews.verdict: Our Danmu API run installed 63 packages in 44 seconds with 0 known vulnerabilities, but there was no build or test target to exercise.
reviews.skip_if: English-only teams: the main and Hugging Face READMEs are Chinese, and no English README is listed at the repository root.

reviews.name: InvisiProxy-Legacy
reviews.verdict: InvisiProxy built in 2 seconds in our sandbox, but its endpoint checks failed after 62 seconds with refused localhost:8080 connections.
reviews.skip_if: New deployments that require an actively maintained starting point: GitHub marks this repository archived, and the README points elsewhere.

reviews.name: docmost
reviews.verdict: Trial Docmost if shared editing matters and your team can operate its database and storage.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring SSO, SCIM provisioning or audit logs in the free edition: the installation guide identifies these as paid features.

reviews.name: wttr.in
reviews.verdict: Consider wttr.in for terminal forecasts and status bars when its documented formats fit your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Operators expecting the example configuration to remove dependence on public wttr.in: it retains that service as its weather source.

reviews.name: Interstellar
reviews.verdict: Trial Interstellar if its bundled interface fits your needs and you can maintain the server.
reviews.skip_if: Users limited to static hosting such as Netlify, Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages.

reviews.name: toolhive
reviews.verdict: Shortlist ToolHive when its shared MCP registry, gateway and local-to-Kubernetes runtime match your requirements.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need evidence of a successful production deployment: our sandbox record provides none.

reviews.name: OpenClash
reviews.verdict: The CodeMirror dependency install recorded 69 dependencies in 43 seconds, while router routing and DNS remained untested.
reviews.skip_if: Desktop users seeking an application for one machine: the documented installation targets OpenWrt and LuCI.

reviews.name: koodo-reader
reviews.verdict: Our Koodo Reader build succeeded in 129 seconds, but the test command found no matching tests, leaving reading and sync behavior unverified in our sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Readers expecting protected Kindle purchases to open directly: the README specifically lists DRM-free Mobipocket and Kindle formats.

reviews.name: rook
reviews.verdict: Rook fits Kubernetes teams that want Ceph's block, file and object storage and can own its operation.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking storage that removes the need to operate Ceph.

reviews.name: openfga
reviews.verdict: Evaluate OpenFGA when relationship-based permissions justify a dedicated authorization engine.
reviews.skip_if: Small applications whose static roles are adequately handled in application code: evaluate whether a separate service adds enough value.

reviews.name: zot
reviews.verdict: Zot merits evaluation for operators who want an OCI registry with configurable storage, authentication and extensions.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a verified installed binary or a measured production workload from this review: our record establishes neither.

reviews.name: limusic
reviews.verdict: Limusic is worth a package-based trial if you want its documented YouTube Music workflow and accept an unofficial client.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs a Google-authorized client Listeners who need playback reliability demonstrated by this review Intel Mac users who require a project-provided binary People expecting Rust dependency downloads alone to produce a working desktop app

reviews.name: arcbox
reviews.verdict: Our ArcBox run spent 587 seconds building before `arcbox-core` failed with Rust error E0308, and the test step hit the same compiler error.
reviews.skip_if: Intel Mac, Windows, or Linux desktop users: the README requires Apple Silicon macOS and describes Intel and Linux host support as future work.

reviews.name: headscale

reviews.name: BillionMail
