reviews.name: d-inference
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Darkbloom if you need to study its provider or network trust model and can test on Apple hardware yourself.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a production recommendation from this review: the measured revision explicitly disclaims production use and support.

reviews.name: deepseek-harness
reviews.verdict: Our DeepSeek Harness build passed in 350 seconds, but its tests timed out at 900 seconds, so we recommend a contained developer evaluation rather than a production commitment.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring stable plugin contracts: the README explicitly warns of compatibility-breaking changes during developer preview.

reviews.name: vllm
reviews.verdict: Consider vLLM when its documented batching and distributed-serving capabilities match a deployment requirement you can test.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a verified throughput, latency, or accelerator-memory benchmark: our run measured none of these.

reviews.name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Single-DGX-Spark-TensorFold
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run this Qwen3.8 Flash Next recipe because Shell is unsupported by the harness and no Dockerfile was detected, so its serving behavior remains unverified by us.
reviews.skip_if: Ordinary CPU servers or small GPU machines: the recipe targets GB10 hardware with 128 GB of unified memory.

reviews.name: ai-native-callcenter
reviews.verdict: Our AI Native Call Center run passed all 72 tests after a 31-second install and a 59-second build, but current reports document silent Qwen campaign endings and missing supervisor browser-phone provisioning.
reviews.skip_if: Unattended Qwen campaigns that require an audible closing line: open issue 207 reports silent hangups after record_lead and hangup at commit 6e2ee1d.

reviews.name: Relate
reviews.verdict: Our Relate run passed all 39 tests, but npm audit reported 4 known vulnerabilities, including 1 critical and 1 high, so I would investigate those findings before importing private chats.
reviews.skip_if: Users who require every conversation to stay on their machine while using a cloud model: the README explicitly allows text to be sent to the AI provider.

reviews.name: vm2api
reviews.verdict: Our vm2api test command ran for 310 seconds and exited 1 despite 9 reported passing tests, while npm audit found 1 moderate vulnerability.
reviews.skip_if: Any business without written permission from the author: the custom license prohibits commercial use, including internal revenue-producing use.

reviews.name: AgentVerse-OS
reviews.verdict: Our AgentVerse OS core build took 150 seconds and all 80 Rust tests passed, which makes the code worth exploring even though the full system is still a single-box alpha.
reviews.skip_if: Teams or families: the README says there are no user accounts or permissions and describes the current system as one person on one server.

reviews.name: superlocal
reviews.verdict: Use SuperLocal as an evaluation checkout if you want to inspect its provider-separated Inbox SDK and fictional-mail demo.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a mail client whose live account workflows this review has verified.

reviews.name: taskview-community
reviews.verdict: Our TaskView install stopped after 1 second because its pnpm 12.6.0 entry file was missing, so a source checkout is not ready to judge by screenshots alone.
reviews.skip_if: Agencies that want to give clients accounts on a shared instance: the license excludes customers and other third parties from permitted users without a separate commercial license.

reviews.name: mlmvpn_windows
reviews.verdict: Our MLMVPN run installed 431 packages, then both the 4-second build and 2-second test command failed, while npm audit found 25 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: macOS or Linux users: the supported application targets Windows 10 and 11, and it needs administrator rights for TUN, firewall, DNS, and route changes.

reviews.name: autobrr
reviews.verdict: Consider autobrr when IRC announcements or a shared filtering layer solve a specific gap in your current download workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Users whose existing *arr feed workflow already meets their needs: autobrr's introduction says another RSS layer is unnecessary when feeding only the *arr applications.

reviews.name: owncast
reviews.verdict: Owncast is worth evaluating for a single broadcaster who wants to operate a streaming page and chat.
reviews.skip_if: Services that need several independent broadcasting accounts within one installation: the README describes a single-user server.

reviews.name: openreplay
reviews.verdict: Shortlist OpenReplay when self-hosted replay, browser context and product analytics match your needs and someone can own the infrastructure.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting our source run to demonstrate a working production deployment: it did not exercise deployment, recording or playback.

reviews.name: NetAlertX
reviews.verdict: NetAlertX is worth a controlled evaluation when device discovery and change alerts are the job.
reviews.skip_if: Operators whose deployment policy forbids the host networking and added capabilities in the documented Docker quick start.

reviews.name: zyfun
reviews.verdict: zyfun is worth evaluating if you already have authorized, compatible sources and can work with its Chinese documentation.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting an included film or channel catalog.

reviews.name: mailflare
reviews.verdict: Our Mailflare install pulled 982 packages and 1,083 MB, then the build stopped after 12 seconds because Wrangler remote mode required a Cloudflare login.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require an OSI-approved open-source license or a normal public-fork contribution flow: the license forbids redistribution and publishing modified copies without permission.

reviews.name: walgit
reviews.verdict: Our walgit build ran for 643 seconds before `walgit-server` failed with 3 compiler errors, and tests hit the same compilation boundary after 271 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a GitHub or GitLab replacement with issues, pull requests, CI, and code review: the README scopes walgit to repository serving and browsing.

reviews.name: evolution-api
reviews.verdict: Evolution API makes sense when its unusually wide set of WhatsApp, webhook, queue, CRM, and storage connections would replace glue code you already expect to maintain.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a clean source build from the measured commit: our build stopped on missing Prisma client exports, including `Contact`, `Message`, `Proxy`, and `Prisma.sql`.

reviews.name: tick-stock-panel
reviews.verdict: Tick Stock Panel is a reasonable candidate for Chinese-reading A-share hobbyists willing to validate a local research setup.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need a verified English onboarding path: the supplied README and deployment guide are in Chinese.

reviews.name: dynamo
reviews.verdict: Evaluate NVIDIA Dynamo when you can name a coordination problem across inference workers, such as independent prefill/decode scaling or routing based on KV-cache overlap.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a verified quick-install result: our recorded run does not establish that Dynamo installed or served requests.

reviews.name: portmaster
reviews.verdict: Portmaster is worth evaluating if you want per-app filtering and encrypted DNS on Windows or Linux, with paid history and SPN available separately.
reviews.skip_if: Readers looking for a documented macOS option: the supplied README describes Windows and Linux desktops.

reviews.name: grok2api
reviews.verdict: Grok2API is worth evaluating when Grok account pooling is the specific requirement and you can manage the documented credential and deployment responsibilities.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking evidence that live Grok requests, media generation, or client integrations worked in our sandbox.

reviews.name: deepseek-whale-girl
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run DeepSeek Whale Girl because its HTML repository has no supported harness ecosystem or Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Product teams expecting all images to inherit MIT permission: the README excludes artwork from the code license and requires source-specific checks.

reviews.name: floorplan-3d
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run floorplan-3d, and its documented route to a custom apartment requires editing data inside index.html.
reviews.skip_if: Homeowners expecting to import an architectural drawing immediately: the README instructs you to edit layout data in the HTML, and issue 10 asks for drawing import.

reviews.name: PDoomVideo
reviews.verdict: Our PDoomVideo run installed 55 packages in 3 seconds, but npm test failed in 1 second because the project supplies only a placeholder test command.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring executable tests before adopting a renderer: npm test is a placeholder that exits with an error.

reviews.name: threejs-architecture-effects
reviews.verdict: threejs-architecture-effects includes an editable, orbitable construction starter, but our lab did not run it because the harness lacked a supported ecosystem and the repo had no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Video producers needing an MP4 exporter or soundtrack: the README says video export and starter music are absent.

reviews.name: vega-app
reviews.verdict: Our Vega App install pulled 1,370 packages and 811 MB, then 6 Jest suites failed and npm audit reported 36 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a ready-made catalog: the README says Vega does not host, store, or provide media, and users manage all third-party sources.

reviews.name: MusicFree
reviews.verdict: Our MusicFree setup stopped after 130 seconds because Yarn saw Node 18.20.8 and `minimatch` required Node 20 or at least 22, so source builders should not trust the stated Node 18 floor without testing their exact lockfile path.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a ready-made streaming catalog: the README says MusicFree includes no music source and depends on plugins for every online result.

reviews.name: Ehviewer_CN_SXJ
reviews.verdict: Our EhViewer build and test steps both ended at `./gradlew: Permission denied`, after 8 and 31 seconds, so source builders should fix and verify the wrapper path before judging the code itself.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users who need full setup and troubleshooting documentation: most of the README, FAQ, and changelog are in Chinese.

reviews.name: scroll-craft
reviews.verdict: The lab found JavaScript but no supported executable target or Dockerfile, so scrollcraft has no independent build or test result on our page.
reviews.skip_if: Developers outside Claude Code who want a documented first-class install path: the README installs it through Claude Code's plugin marketplace.

reviews.name: webpack
reviews.verdict: webpack is worth retaining or evaluating when its loaders, plugins and chunk controls answer a concrete build requirement.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners whose priority is minimal configuration: webpack's README describes it as a low-level tool that is not always the easiest entry-level solution.

reviews.name: nuxt
reviews.verdict: Nuxt is worth evaluating for a Vue team that wants integrated routing, several rendering modes, and server code.
reviews.skip_if: Teams committed to a different component framework and unwilling to adopt Vue.

reviews.name: video-prediction-policy-2
reviews.verdict: Our VPP2 sandbox installed successfully in 63 seconds and built in 1 second, but the authors withhold the distilled planner and Stage-3 policy behind their reported real-world results.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need to reproduce the headline real-world policy: the authors have no plans to release its distilled planner and Stage-3 components.

reviews.name: muse-gadget-sdk
reviews.verdict: Our Linux source run installed in 24 seconds and built in 1 second, but the test command exited 1 with 79 failures and 56 errors.
reviews.skip_if: Offline-assistant builders: the gadget connects to hosted Muse rather than running its model locally.

reviews.name: 3dicon
reviews.verdict: Trial 3dicon for a reviewed animated app icon if hosted generation fits your workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring offline generation: the documented workflow uses hosted image and video services.

reviews.name: DeepSelect
reviews.verdict: Trial DeepSelect only when its documented TopK contract fits your workload and you can qualify it on the intended hardware.
reviews.skip_if: Applications requiring topk values above 4096 or input types outside the documented paths.

reviews.name: MemOS
reviews.verdict: Evaluate MemOS when editable memory and memory-cube isolation justify its operating requirements.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a clean test result before adoption: our recorded Python test command exited with code 1.

reviews.name: AI-Engineering-Coach
reviews.verdict: Consider AI Engineer Coach for a personal trial if inspecting coaching rules alongside the sessions they flag would help you.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a ready-to-install Marketplace or Releases package.

reviews.name: GameFactory-3A
reviews.verdict: Trial GameFactory-3A with an engineer responsible for the selected engine, model environment and acceptance evidence.
reviews.skip_if: Creators expecting installation alone to produce a finished game.

reviews.name: robin
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Robin for source-checked dark-web leads if you can operate Tor, control model access and preserve original material.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring demonstrated live onion-search reliability before adoption; our recorded run does not establish it.

reviews.name: godogen
reviews.verdict: Godogen is worth a supervised prototype trial if you want an agent to assemble a game project and you can evaluate the result.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking measured evidence that Godogen reliably produces finished games: our run did not test that outcome.

reviews.name: oil-motion
reviews.verdict: Oil Motion warrants a supervised pilot when the central effect needs changing subject imagery and direct user control.
reviews.skip_if: Projects needing only interface transitions, button feedback, or layout motion that ordinary frontend code can handle.

reviews.name: computer
reviews.verdict: Use Cloudflare Computer when durable agent files on Workers are central to the application and its stable filesystem or Worker JavaScript backend fits the task.
reviews.skip_if: Production applications that require the experimental Worker shell, ContainerBackend or synchronization protocol.

reviews.name: agent-of-empires
reviews.verdict: Agent of Empires is worth evaluating when you need management features around several persistent coding-agent sessions.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a coding agent or model: this is a session manager around separately launched tools.

reviews.name: douyin-downloader
reviews.verdict: Do not choose the Python CLI for dependable everyday Douyin downloads while its documented verification block persists.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs reliable unattended downloads of individual videos, photos, collections, music, likes or favorites while the documented verification block persists.

reviews.name: corsair
reviews.verdict: Corsair merits a provider-specific evaluation if you want one integration layer for application code and agents.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a successful full-repository build and test run before evaluation: our recorded commands did not meet that condition.

reviews.name: WeMM-Embedding
reviews.verdict: Trial WeMM-Embedding for retrieval across text and visual media if you can validate the model on your corpus and hardware.
reviews.skip_if: Applications that require audio embeddings.

reviews.name: Kronos
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Kronos as a specialized forecasting candidate once you can defend the checkpoint's evaluation window.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a ready-to-deploy trading strategy with validated returns after costs.

reviews.name: evilginx2
reviews.verdict: Our Evilginx sandbox built in 27 seconds, but its successful test command reported zero tests, leaving assessment behavior unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing the public maintainer to supply or create phishlets: the README explicitly declines that support.

reviews.name: codegraph
reviews.verdict: The successful install and build support a contained evaluation of CodeGraph at commit 00d7430.
reviews.skip_if: Release owners requiring a passing verification baseline: the recorded test command exited 1.

reviews.name: hop
reviews.verdict: Evaluate HOP on copies of your documents if opening HWP/HWPX and saving HWP meet your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Workflows that require HWPX saving or autosave/recovery; the supplied development guide says these are unavailable.

reviews.name: TensorFold
reviews.verdict: Evaluate TensorFold when your chosen release documents the checkpoint and hardware you intend to use.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking measured inference speed, usable context or serving memory requirements from this sandbox run.

reviews.name: cve-mcp-server
reviews.verdict: CVE MCP Server has a documented role in consolidating vulnerability research, but our run did not establish a working analyst workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a working installation without dependency investigation: our sandbox captured an MCP 2.x import failure during server startup.

reviews.name: LunaTV
reviews.verdict: Try LunaTV if you can maintain a private Docker deployment and already have authorized source APIs.
reviews.skip_if: Readers expecting an included catalog or ready-to-watch deployment Operators seeking evidence of tested playback, concurrency or production reliability Commercial or public-service deployments: the README explicitly prohibits these uses

reviews.name: ming-official-atlas
reviews.verdict: Use Ming Official Atlas as a browsing aid for Ming institutions, with historical checks at the individual-record level.
reviews.skip_if: Researchers who require a complete annual roster of Ming officials.

reviews.name: BeefTV
reviews.verdict: Our BeefTV backend built in 101 seconds, but its tests timed out at 900 seconds with 17 passes and 4 failures reported.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a green backend suite: our run timed out at 900 seconds with 17 passes and 4 failures reported.

reviews.name: livecanvas
reviews.verdict: LiveCanvas supplies a silent H.264-and-JPEG pairing workflow, but its README explicitly stops short of automatic iPhone Photos import.
reviews.skip_if: Creators needing audio in the supplied Live Photo path: the README and pairing guide restrict it to silent H.264 video with JPEG images.

reviews.name: DeepEP-Ascend
reviews.verdict: Our DeepEP-Ascend test command ended with 12 collection/setup errors and no executed pass or failure results, despite successful install and build steps.
reviews.skip_if: NVIDIA-only deployments: this backend targets Ascend 950 hardware, while the original DeepEP is the NVIDIA route.

reviews.name: jeeves
reviews.verdict: Our Jeeves install used 5,696 MB for 98 packages and passed its build, but our sandbox skipped tests and did not validate inference.
reviews.skip_if: CPU-only servers: the documented quick start requires CUDA, with Apple Silicon as the other stated inference route.

reviews.name: product-film-skill
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run Product Film because its harness had no supported execution path for the TypeScript checkout, so we cannot vouch for a finished render.
reviews.skip_if: Claude chat-app users: the README requires Claude Code running a local toolchain and explicitly excludes the chat apps.

reviews.name: shipvideo
reviews.verdict: Our Shipvideo run installed 39 packages in 15 seconds and passed its build in 5 seconds, but had no test target and did not establish a completed video render.
reviews.skip_if: Projects requiring included music, recorded footage, or a talking presenter: the scene tool rejects audio and video elements.

reviews.name: FounderOS
reviews.verdict: Our FounderOS install took 29 seconds, but npm audit reported 66 vulnerabilities, including 1 critical and 52 high, and build and tests were skipped.
reviews.skip_if: Founders expecting an npm-only desktop app: the README requires PostgreSQL with pgvector, Redis, Go, and the Elixir knowledge engine.

reviews.name: G0DM0D3
reviews.verdict: Our G0DM0D3 run installed 817 packages and used 592 MB, then failed its 44-second build while npm audit reported 31 vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a green production build: our Next.js build failed on a TypeScript Map iteration error at commit f630176.

reviews.name: editaplot2026
reviews.verdict: Our EditaPlot run installed 35 packages and built successfully, but the 291-test run ended with 19 failures and 34 collection/setup errors, so this is a promising specialist tool that is not ready for a blind rollout.
reviews.skip_if: Mac, Linux, WSL, Wine, Parallels, or virtual-machine users: the README says the full Origin path is supported only on physical Windows 10/11 x64 computers.

reviews.name: post-production-skill
reviews.verdict: Our lab could not run this 15.3 MB prompt bundle because it has no supported executable ecosystem or Dockerfile, and the repository supplies no automated checks.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting video generation or editing: the skill outputs one prompt and does not submit a generation job by default.

reviews.name: uplifting-biomolecular-modeling
reviews.verdict: Our `af2ig/opt/` run installed 36 packages in 27 seconds and built in 4 seconds, but it ran 0 tests and exercised no GPU inference.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require upstream support or ongoing fixes: Anthropic labels this a reference release, says it is not maintained, and does not accept contributions.

reviews.name: jev-review
reviews.verdict: Our Jev Review install took 3 seconds and npm audit found 0 known vulnerabilities, but the repository had no build or test target and whole-codebase review followed at most 8 signals.
reviews.skip_if: Go, Rust, Python, Java, or mixed-language repositories: the source discovery pattern accepts only JavaScript and TypeScript extensions.

reviews.name: video-generator-client
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 51 packages, built in 7 seconds, and passed all 4 tests in 9 seconds, which makes Video Generator Client easy to inspect and try.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a stable model catalog: the README and `catalog.py` list different model IDs, and open pull request 2 exists to reconcile them.

reviews.name: haiming-app-monetization
reviews.verdict: Our lab could not run Haiming App Monetization because the repository has no supported ecosystem or Dockerfile, so v0.1.0 should be judged as a four-file advice package rather than working monetization software.
reviews.skip_if: English-only teams: the README, skill, acceptance cases, and default prompt are Chinese, with no English guide.

reviews.name: itsgiving
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 61 packages into 978 MB and found 2 known vulnerabilities, while the repository supplied no test target, so It's Giving is a playful source project rather than meeting-ready software.
reviews.skip_if: Work meetings where a false reaction would be costly: the README warns that effects fire automatically and everyone sees the result.

reviews.name: mobilecode
reviews.verdict: Our MobileCode install took 94 seconds, added 2,362 packages, and used 2,470 MB, while the root test command deliberately refused to run package tests.
reviews.skip_if: iOS developers working from Linux or Windows: iOS preview requires macOS and Xcode.

reviews.name: image-to-3d-pipeline
reviews.verdict: Our build of the 70 MB web explorer passed in 14 seconds with 0 audit findings, but the complete reconstruction stack has no unified install or test target.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting one command to install and run the complete reconstruction stack: `setup.sh` only clones 4 upstream tools, while their Python environments and model weights remain separate.

reviews.name: BrowserKitten
reviews.verdict: BrowserKitten is a candidate for a supervised trial when operating inside an already logged-in Chrome session is the requirement.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who require a Chrome Web Store installation: the README explicitly says the extension is not on the store.

reviews.name: interdimensional-game
reviews.verdict: Our LAST FRAME install pulled 307 packages and used 604 MB, then built in 30 seconds, but it offered no test target and npm reported one high and one moderate vulnerability.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need code they can legally reuse or redistribute: the repository has no detected license, so default copyright restrictions apply.

reviews.name: infinite-livestream
reviews.verdict: Our FastH3 install took 124 seconds and its 1-second build passed, but pytest executed no tests because `numpy` was missing during collection.
reviews.skip_if: Ordinary self-hosters: the model README calls for four NVIDIA B200 GPUs, CUDA 13, and roughly 148 GB of weights.

reviews.name: mindcraft
reviews.verdict: Our Mindcraft install failed after 113 seconds because its Mineflayer patch targeted 4.33.0 while npm installed 4.39.0, so commit 5f3acc8 is not a clean-start recommendation.
reviews.skip_if: Public-server operators who want coding enabled: the README warns that prompt injection can lead the model to execute code on the host.

reviews.name: sdf-js
reviews.verdict: Our sdf-js run installed 116 packages in 14 seconds and passed its tests in 31 seconds, but npm audit found 2 high-severity vulnerabilities and no build target existed.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial product teams without a separate agreement: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 covers the Atlas code and COMMERCIAL.md says commercial use requires another license.

reviews.name: gsd-core
reviews.verdict: GSD Core merits a trial for projects that need persistent planning records and a repeatable agent workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring evidence of a completed end-to-end agent workflow before adoption: our run covered repository setup, build, and an incomplete test command.

reviews.name: GamePhanes
reviews.verdict: Use GamePhanes to inspect and develop runtime acceptance contracts for game-project repairs.
reviews.skip_if: Researchers who need our run to establish game-engine performance or agent repair ability: it covers the repository's Node test command.

reviews.name: personaplex
reviews.verdict: Evaluate PersonaPlex when overlapping speech and prompted voice or role control are central to your project.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting this review's successful client build to establish working model inference or real-time audio performance.

reviews.name: OpenCluely
reviews.verdict: Evaluate OpenCluely only for permitted practice where its floating answer window serves a specific need and you can investigate setup.
reviews.skip_if: Candidates whose interview rules prohibit outside assistance.

reviews.name: miles
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Miles when you need configurable model post-training infrastructure and can validate the chosen GPU environment.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a verified laptop walkthrough: the documented Qwen3-4B quick start specifies eight H100, H200 or B-series GPUs and at least 500 GB of free disk.

reviews.name: Code-as-World
reviews.verdict: Our 3-CPU, 8 GB sandbox produced no install, build, or test result for commit 87d4159 because the lab lacked a supported Python ecosystem and the repo had no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need a CPU setup: the README requires Python 3.10 or 3.11 on a CUDA host, and its serving recipe uses vLLM with GPU memory settings.

reviews.name: GamePhanes
reviews.verdict: Consider GamePhanes, now presented as GameForgeBench, when your research needs game-project repairs checked through runtime behavior.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking measured agent-repair performance from our review: our run did not evaluate a coding agent.

reviews.name: PRAXIST
reviews.verdict: PRAXIST is worth a bounded evaluation when you already own a runnable research project, a credible evaluator, and an operating budget.
reviews.skip_if: Projects without a runnable baseline or measurable evaluation path.

reviews.name: tutti
reviews.verdict: Tutti is worth evaluating if you regularly carry context between supported agents.
reviews.skip_if: People who need a Linux desktop download from the supplied Quick Start: it lists macOS and Windows, but no Linux package.

reviews.name: GPT-SoVITS
reviews.verdict: Shortlist GPT-SoVITS for an attended dubbing workflow that needs recording preparation and reference-based speech.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring measured synthesis quality or throughput before choosing a tool: our run contains neither measurement.

reviews.name: biosecurity-agent
reviews.verdict: Biosecurity Agent version 0.1.2 is worth evaluating as a supervised evidence-workflow experiment: our recorded install, build and test commands succeeded.
reviews.skip_if: People seeking clinical diagnosis: the pinned README explicitly excludes that purpose.

reviews.name: cloudflare-os
reviews.verdict: Cloudflare OS is worth a bounded engineering pilot if personal AI-built applications and explicit service permissions match your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Nontechnical teams expecting a finished office suite with little operational work Organizations requiring a documented production deployment on their own servers today; the supplied README marks that tooling and guidance as coming soon Buyers requiring independently verified isolation, integration reliability…

reviews.name: Pentest-Swarm-AI
reviews.verdict: Pentest Swarm AI is a reasonable candidate for a supervised lab evaluation if its shared-board architecture interests you.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone without explicit written permission to test the target Teams requiring independently demonstrated autonomous assessment quality Buyers who need verified scope enforcement, report accuracy or production reliability before adoption Operators unable to isolate tool execution and review consequential actions

reviews.name: Open-Generative-AI
reviews.verdict: Open Generative AI is worth evaluating when you want its Muapi interface or selected desktop local engines.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need this recorded checkout to pass a production build without further investigation.

reviews.name: cwc-workshops
reviews.verdict: Use cwc-workshops for exercises you are prepared to verify and maintain.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a maintained production starter or upstream maintenance support.

reviews.name: deepwiki-rs
reviews.verdict: Litho is worth a limited trial if you want model-generated C4 documentation and can review the result.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require verified sentence-level source citations before accepting generated claims.

reviews.name: plandex
reviews.verdict: Plandex merits a restricted evaluation if its plan-and-diff workflow fits your work and you can operate the local server.
reviews.skip_if: New users seeking Plandex Cloud: the README says it began winding down on October 3, 2025 and no longer accepts new users.

reviews.name: orca
reviews.verdict: Orca is worth evaluating if comparing several CLI-agent attempts in separate worktrees is a recurring task.
reviews.skip_if: Developers whose existing single-agent terminal workflow already meets their needs.

reviews.name: QuantDinger
reviews.verdict: QuantDinger is worth evaluating for Python research and paper trading if your team can operate its service stack.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking investment advice, guaranteed returns, or an unattended profitable trading system.

reviews.name: OpenMetadata
reviews.verdict: OpenMetadata is worth evaluating when a platform team needs catalog discovery, lineage, quality, governance, and assistant access to maintained metadata.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing a local trial below the documented Docker allocation of 6 GiB of memory and 4 vCPUs.

reviews.name: MaxKB
reviews.verdict: MaxKB is worth a focused trial if its documented combination of RAG, workflows, and MCP tools matches your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who need demonstrated retrieval quality, provider compatibility, or production capacity from this review: our run measured repository setup only.

reviews.name: OmniRoute
reviews.verdict: Our OmniRoute source build failed after 32 seconds, and tests timed out at 900 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting installation to grant free tokens: provider accounts and eligibility remain separate requirements.

reviews.name: cc-switch
reviews.verdict: CC Switch is worth evaluating when changing providers and maintaining configuration across several coding tools has become routine work.
reviews.skip_if: Users whose operating system does not meet the documented requirements: Windows 10+, macOS 12+, or Linux with glibc 2.35+ and WebKitGTK 4.1.

reviews.name: wenzi-xiaohongshu-workflow
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run Wenzi's skills pack because no supported ecosystem or Dockerfile was available, so neither agent behavior nor publishing outcomes were verified.
reviews.skip_if: English-only teams: the README and inspected skill bodies are Chinese, with no English README listed.

reviews.name: turnstile-token

reviews.skip_if: Presenters who want to arrange every animation visually without writing scene code: the starting workflow uses a Python class and terminal command.

reviews.name: d2
reviews.verdict: Evaluate D2 for diagrams maintained alongside code and for its documented export formats.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a successful source test command before adoption: the measured command exited 1, and the retained tail does not explain why.

reviews.name: magika
reviews.verdict: Use Magika when textual file labels improve editor behavior or scanner routing and your team can evaluate representative inputs.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a file-type prediction to guarantee upload safety.

reviews.name: linux
reviews.verdict: Use torvalds/linux for kernel source investigation and development.
reviews.skip_if: People expecting torvalds/linux to supply a complete desktop installer.

reviews.name: lerna
reviews.verdict: Our Lerna source build passed in 41 seconds and its test step passed in 113 seconds, while the checkout audit reported 76 vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: New workspaces choosing a build and release platform from scratch: the maintainers recommend Nx directly.

reviews.name: BongoCat
reviews.verdict: Our BongoCat build failed after 223 seconds at an rfd Linux backend requirement.
reviews.skip_if: Linux users seeking a documented release target: the contributor guide explicitly excludes Linux.

reviews.name: drawio-desktop
reviews.verdict: Use draw.io Desktop for offline local-file diagrams when its documented package choices and repository-based support fit your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose essential workflow is the browser editor's cloud storage and sharing, which desktop hides.

reviews.name: open-source-mac-os-apps
reviews.verdict: Use open-source-mac-os-apps if you want application candidates, macOS codebases to explore or a catalog to contribute to.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking tested rankings of individual Mac applications.

reviews.name: FlClash
reviews.verdict: Our FlClash source install failed after 27 seconds at a missing local module file, leaving packaged-app behavior unassessed.
reviews.skip_if: iPhone users who require a documented upstream iOS package: the README lists none.

reviews.name: validator
reviews.verdict: Use go-playground/validator when Go request structs define your input contract and your team can represent missing values explicitly.
reviews.skip_if: APIs that expect required on a plain bool to accept false while also detecting omission without changing the request model.

reviews.name: rustlings
reviews.verdict: Use Rustlings if you want small Rust exercises alongside the Book and learn well from compiler feedback.
reviews.skip_if: Readers whose main need is guidance on designing larger applications.

reviews.name: trpc
reviews.verdict: Our source build succeeded in 12 seconds, but the test command exited 1 with 1,998 passes and one release-test timeout.
reviews.skip_if: Next.js teams whose Server Components already solve their data needs: [the official RSC guide says tRPC may be unnecessary](research:e17a7782a2280b70#page-4).

reviews.name: awesome-python
reviews.verdict: Use Awesome Python to form a shortlist for a Python task, then verify each candidate's compatibility and fit.
reviews.skip_if: Readers needing an exhaustive catalog: the policy limits entries per use case.

reviews.name: wloc
reviews.verdict: Use Yu9191/wloc to investigate network-location rewriting on a spare iPhone you control if you can diagnose proxy traffic and certificate errors.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing dependable location changes on an everyday phone.

reviews.name: requests
reviews.verdict: Use Requests for synchronous Python scripts and integrations needing HTTP/1.1 calls, Sessions and streamed responses.
reviews.skip_if: Applications requiring native asynchronous HTTP calls or HTTP/2: HTTPX documents both capabilities.

reviews.name: Recordly
reviews.verdict: Recordly passed 1,463 tests in our sandbox, but its 150-second build failed during Linux packaging with a missing GitHub token error.
reviews.skip_if: Linux creators who require a single polished pointer: the README says exports can show the real cursor and the rendered overlay together.

reviews.name: julia
reviews.verdict: Use Julia when numerical modeling is your work and you can check the calculations and package combinations you depend on.
reviews.skip_if: Researchers whose deadlines leave no room to investigate gradient errors or package interactions.

reviews.name: difftastic
reviews.verdict: Our Difftastic build succeeded in 176 seconds and Cargo test recorded 294 passed with 0 failed, supporting a trial as a second view for code review.
reviews.skip_if: Workflows that need an applicable patch: generating patches is an explicit non-goal.

reviews.name: obs-studio
reviews.verdict: Our 6-second npm step covered OBS's RTMP service-data directory, and the later desktop attempt stopped at the lab's Compose-file requirement.
reviews.skip_if: People seeking a video editor for timeline trimming and cutting: OBS composes and captures, while the recording tutorial sends viewers to a separate editor.

reviews.name: comprehensive-rust
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox built Google's Rust course in 117 seconds and recorded 107 passed, 0 failed, so its repository is a credible starting point for preparing a class.
reviews.skip_if: First-time programmers: the stated audience is experienced software engineers, typically coming from C++ or Java.

reviews.name: awesome-cpp
reviews.verdict: Use awesome-cpp to discover C and C++ library candidates when you can assess the upstream projects yourself.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need uniform per-project stars, update dates and language-standard tags: issue #917 requests those additions.

reviews.name: filament
reviews.verdict: Our Filament documentation-tooling run recorded 0 tests and exited 5, so it supplies no rendering verdict.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a unified game-making interface: the README shows application-owned scene and frame setup.

reviews.name: serverless
reviews.verdict: Our source install took 19 seconds, but the test command failed after 166 seconds; the November CLI run separately completed the updater on Framework 4.46.0.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations requiring a wholly permissive CLI distribution: the README distinguishes MIT source from proprietary components in the npm module.

reviews.name: godot
reviews.verdict: Use Godot Engine when its reusable scenes, MIT license, language workflow, and export paths fit your game.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring Godot 4 C# browser exports through the standard export path.

reviews.name: wasmer
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Wasmer when your application needs embedded execution of packaged programs with explicit host access, and account for the sandbox SDK's alpha status.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring unchanged Linux workload compatibility.

reviews.name: leetcode
reviews.verdict: Use doocs/leetcode's English topic links and worked explanations after attempting a problem yourself.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need this review to establish solution correctness: the sandbox test step was skipped.

reviews.name: CyberChef
reviews.verdict: Our source run installed in 28 seconds and passed tests in 21 seconds, but its production build failed after 245 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a clean source production build from our tested configuration: the build exited 3, despite successful installation and tests.

reviews.name: chinese-independent-developer
reviews.verdict: Use chinese-independent-developer to discover Chinese makers' products or prepare your own submission.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who require independently tested product recommendations.

reviews.name: system-design-101
reviews.verdict: Use System Design 101 if you want visual introductions before deeper study.
reviews.skip_if: Candidates who want a sequenced practice course with worked answers: System Design Primer explicitly supplies questions and sample solutions.

reviews.name: lede
reviews.verdict: Our LEDE build exited 1 after 7 seconds, so this run does not establish a usable firmware image.
reviews.skip_if: WSL users keeping the checkout on a case-insensitive filesystem: the README documents a build restriction.

reviews.name: Wox
reviews.verdict: Our Wox run built successfully in 27 seconds and passed 2 Go tests, which supports a source-workflow trial but leaves desktop behavior unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Windows users who need a guaranteed stable experience across mixed-scale monitors: issue 4680 reports misplaced UI in v2.4.8, with a maintainer pointing to a development-build fix.

reviews.name: ImHex
reviews.verdict: Choose ImHex for repeated binary-format investigation where reusable patterns and linked displays serve the work.
reviews.skip_if: People who only need a quick byte patch: ExeDepot recommends HxD as easier to learn for that job.

reviews.name: refined-github
reviews.verdict: Our Refined GitHub run built in 15 seconds and passed its test command with 629 Vitest passes and 28 skips, making this a credible source snapshot to evaluate.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need GitHub to look exactly like the standard interface: the extension changes controls, layout and shortcuts across the site.

reviews.name: devdocs
reviews.verdict: Our DevDocs sandbox passed 41 Node tests in 3 seconds, but those checks did not establish a working Ruby service or scraper.
reviews.skip_if: Learners expecting a programming course or broad web search: the README excludes guides and search-engine coverage from its scope.

reviews.name: FFmpeg
reviews.verdict: Our FFmpeg source install stopped after 3 seconds at the NASM check, so this run supports a setup finding rather than a conversion benchmark.
reviews.skip_if: Users who want ordinary video conversion without command syntax: HandBrake offers a graphical route.

reviews.name: cs249r_book
reviews.verdict: Machine Learning Systems installed in 107 seconds and built in 4 seconds in our sandbox, but its test command ended with 17 failures.
reviews.skip_if: Instructors needing stable agentic or physical-AI textbooks: the README calls Volumes III and IV open drafts and asks readers not to teach or cite them yet.

reviews.name: shadPS4
reviews.verdict: Our shadPS4 run installed 151 dependencies in a nested documentation project and skipped build and tests.
reviews.skip_if: People expecting this core repository to include a graphical interface.

reviews.name: croc
reviews.verdict: Use croc for occasional code-based handoffs when the recipient can follow the receiving procedure and you can check delivery.
reviews.skip_if: People choosing a transfer tool primarily for unattended replacement of changing files.

reviews.name: brew
reviews.verdict: Use Homebrew for reusable workstation software inventories when rolling updates are acceptable.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a Brewfile to recreate exact historical versions: Bundle has no version lock file.

reviews.name: SecLists
reviews.verdict: Our November attempt stopped at install planning after cloning; the October harness did not run the collection.
reviews.skip_if: People expecting a guided scanner: SecLists supplies input files, while another tool makes requests and interprets responses Operators who want to store testing payloads on important servers: the README explicitly warns against that location Teams requiring every XSS reference file…

reviews.name: Karabiner-Elements
reviews.verdict: Our Karabiner-Elements run installed only the vendored debugger's dependencies, with 28 npm advisories and no native app build or runtime verification.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users: the README's supported systems are macOS only.

reviews.name: Proton
reviews.verdict: Our Proton component build failed after 31 seconds because pkg-config could not find gstreamer-1.0, leaving the supported full build and game compatibility unassessed.
reviews.skip_if: Players who only want to launch a game and are considering compiling first: Valve explicitly recommends Steam's supplied Proton for most users.

reviews.name: obsidian-releases
reviews.verdict: Use Obsidian Releases to inspect release metadata and the documented extension-distribution rules.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking Obsidian's application source code.

reviews.name: pyrefly
reviews.verdict: Our Pyrefly source build took 307 seconds, and tests timed out after 900 seconds without a complete suite result.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting strict semantic-versioning guarantees: Pyrefly says any version may introduce new type errors or breaking changes.

reviews.name: Wand-Enhancer
reviews.verdict: Our WandEnhancer sandbox passed all 49 web-panel tests, but it provides no Windows patcher compatibility result.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing an official executable download: the README says releases contain notes only and directs users to their own Actions artifacts.

reviews.name: airgorah
reviews.verdict: Consider Airgorah if you own the network, use Linux, have compatible wireless hardware and want graphical auditing controls.
reviews.skip_if: Android users looking for an upstream application: the README specifies Linux.

reviews.name: bettercap
reviews.verdict: Bettercap merits a controlled evaluation for authorized work that needs its documented active network functions.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring verified compilation and a clean test baseline from this review.

reviews.name: bubbletea
reviews.verdict: Our source build passed in 14 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Applications requiring dependable native bitmap display across terminals: image support request #163 remains open in the checked issue history.

reviews.name: wezterm
reviews.verdict: Our WezTerm build failed after 267 seconds because pkg-config could not find x11-xcb, and the test command stopped at the same requirement.
reviews.skip_if: Users who want to manage every preference through a graphical editor: the documented configuration workflow uses Lua.

reviews.name: devspace
reviews.verdict: Our DevSpace source run passed all 147 tests, while the later library recipe stopped without completing a coding task.
reviews.skip_if: Unattended workflows requiring automatic recovery of a committed operation whose response was lost: #334 closed the proposed recovery design as not planned.

reviews.name: monaco-editor
reviews.verdict: Our source run installed in 24 seconds and passed its build and test steps, giving Monaco a successful contributor baseline at ba7a57d.
reviews.skip_if: Products that require phone or tablet browser editing: Microsoft explicitly excludes mobile browser support.

reviews.name: zod
reviews.verdict: Use Zod when you control application schemas and want runtime validation with inferred TypeScript types.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring unchanged Zod 3 function-valued configuration: issue #4143 reports wrapper failures, including missing validation and errors inside unions.

reviews.name: waveterm
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Wave Terminal if remote editing and previews address a recurring task.
reviews.skip_if: Users requiring verified desktop installation, interactive SSH recovery or AI behavior before choosing a terminal.

reviews.name: tech-interview-handbook
reviews.verdict: Use the hosted Tech Interview Handbook if you want a free roadmap through coding practice, resumes and interview preparation.
reviews.skip_if: Front-end candidates seeking their entire curriculum in this handbook: upstream directs that material to Front End Interview Handbook.

reviews.name: i-have-adhd
reviews.verdict: Use i-have-adhd for switchable, action-first output on work you can judge yourself.
reviews.skip_if: Reviewers who need exhaustive findings and do not want to inspect or change the list-cap rule after reports of omitted items.

reviews.name: awesome-rust
reviews.verdict: Our source build succeeded in 105 seconds, but cargo test ran zero tests: this result supports compilation of the directory’s maintenance code.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting inclusion to certify current maintenance: the removal policy retains projects until outright breakage or declared deprecation.

reviews.name: bevy
reviews.verdict: Use Bevy if you want Rust, ECS composition and control over custom authoring tools, and can budget for API migrations.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need established visual authoring workflows immediately for a substantial 3D game.

reviews.name: ghidra
reviews.verdict: Our Ghidra install step succeeded in 23 seconds, but the build and test steps each failed after 11 seconds, with the test log recording a Gradle download timeout.
reviews.skip_if: Embedded-debugging teams that need a proven M1 launch path immediately: issue #7217 records a traceRMI timeout before GDB becomes usable.

reviews.name: kilocode
reviews.verdict: Our Kilo Code install recorded 1,996 dependencies and 2,629 MB, while the root test command refused to run tests.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors expecting a root test command to validate the checkout: ours explicitly refused to run tests there.

reviews.name: mermaid
reviews.verdict: Use Mermaid when developers maintain diagram definitions alongside reviewed documentation and automatic layout suits the drawing.
reviews.skip_if: Authors who require exact placement and manual connection routing; SimpleMermaid's comparison describes Draw.io's controls for that work.

reviews.name: compose
reviews.verdict: Use Docker Compose to share a Docker application's service configuration for development, CI or a deliberately managed single host.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring workload placement across multiple hosts: Docker documents Compose's production role as single-host deployment.

reviews.name: zoxide
reviews.verdict: Our zoxide run built in 27 seconds and passed all 18 reported tests; the separate quick-start recipe stopped before a directory jump.
reviews.skip_if: Users who require every short query to keep selecting an identical destination: ranked matches change with directory history.

reviews.name: open-slide
reviews.verdict: Our Open Slide sandbox passed all 455 tests.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require native editable objects in Open Slide's PowerPoint exports.

reviews.name: podman
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Podman for rootless Linux containers when its documented host requirements fit your application.
reviews.skip_if: Kubernetes operators selecting a CRI implementation: Podman explicitly excludes that interface from its scope.

reviews.name: googletest
reviews.verdict: Use GoogleTest if your C++ team wants assertions, fixtures and GoogleMock together and can maintain test linking and runner registration.
reviews.skip_if: Educators expecting GoogleTest alone to interrupt hung submissions safely: issue #348 records a maintainer declining built-in timeouts.

reviews.name: lvgl
reviews.verdict: Shortlist LVGL for a C-based interface when the team can own display integration and UI locking.
reviews.skip_if: Firmware architectures that cannot serialize UI access: LVGL is not thread-safe.

reviews.name: tldr
reviews.verdict: Use tldr pages through a client when you need common command examples; skip it as your sole reference if exhaustive option coverage is essential.
reviews.skip_if: Readers needing exhaustive option coverage: the README describes a complement to man pages.

reviews.name: cpython
reviews.verdict: Our CPython documentation-path install took 11 seconds and its build took 1 second, with tests skipped, so the useful result is a successful documentation workflow rather than a validated interpreter build.
reviews.skip_if: Application developers seeking a settled production interpreter from the development branch: the current README labels main an alpha development version.

reviews.name: flow
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Flow for an existing Flow codebase or a project that deliberately wants its checking model and syntax.
reviews.skip_if: Projects that cannot configure a compiler to remove Flow annotations before execution.

reviews.name: folly
reviews.verdict: Our Folly Python run ended with 2 collection/setup errors after a successful 20-second install, leaving the native C++ library unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Distributors requiring binary compatibility across library updates: Folly explicitly makes no ABI compatibility guarantee between commits.

reviews.name: ghostty
reviews.verdict: Use Ghostty when native macOS or Linux tabs, splits, terminal images or remote clipboard workflows address a specific need.
reviews.skip_if: Developers requiring a native Windows desktop application: Ghostty's feature documentation lists macOS and Linux and describes Windows support as planned.

reviews.name: OpenSpec
reviews.verdict: Use OpenSpec when durable requirements and a human review before implementation justify maintaining planning files.
reviews.skip_if: Developers whose small fixes or visual experiments do not justify a separate proposal review.

reviews.name: insomnia
reviews.verdict: Use Insomnia for reusable authenticated API requests if your team accepts Kong's account requirements and documented storage choices.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring most capabilities without a vendor account: the README identifies Scratch Pad as the account-free route.

reviews.name: awesome-react-native
reviews.verdict: Use jondot/awesome-react-native to shortlist React Native libraries and find learning material.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting a starter application to clone and run.

reviews.name: nippo
reviews.verdict: Nippo passed all 85 tests in our November 25 source run, while the separate quickstart stopped before collecting history or generating a report.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing exhaustive autonomous-work accounting: default filtering removes sessions with no meaningful user prompt remaining.

reviews.name: hiring-without-whiteboards
reviews.verdict: In our run, repository installation took 5 seconds and the test step passed in 2 seconds; those results describe a checkout, not employer behavior.
reviews.skip_if: Candidates who require no live coding: the README explicitly permits pairing.

reviews.name: magic-wormhole
reviews.verdict: Magic Wormhole is worth evaluating for an occasional, coordinated file handoff.
reviews.skip_if: Senders who need recipients to collect a file after the sender disconnects: both clients must remain running until completion.

reviews.name: cmux
reviews.verdict: Our cmux run installed 457 dependencies in 36 seconds, but skipped build and tests, leaving the Mac application unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Linux and Windows desktop users: the README limits the native application to macOS.

reviews.name: floci
reviews.verdict: The Floci CDK compatibility subproject built in 16 seconds, but tests were skipped and npm audit reported 1 high-severity vulnerability.
reviews.skip_if: Speech workflows requiring actual transcription: the README says Transcribe jobs complete immediately without real audio processing.

reviews.name: radare2
reviews.verdict: Our radare2 npm build failed after 163 seconds at a permission-denied installation step, and its test command could not find the run target.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a graphical-first interface in the core tool: the README introduces terminal commands and lists iaito separately as its official Qt interface.

reviews.name: lima
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Lima when you want to configure Linux VMs directly for local development.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a container-focused starting point with documented runtime defaults should compare Colima.

reviews.name: gleam
reviews.verdict: The October 6 compiler checkout built in 250 seconds, but 16 of 12,240 tests failed.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring this measured compiler checkout to pass every test before starting work: the sandbox run recorded 16 failures.

reviews.name: iina
reviews.verdict: Use IINA if you want mpv playback with native Mac controls, subtitles, playlists and configurable plugins.
reviews.skip_if: Windows users choosing an application for their own desktop Viewers whose essential requirement is direct AirPlay or Chromecast sending Researchers choosing specifically for persistent custom bookmarks People looking for a trim-and-split video editor

reviews.name: Mole
reviews.verdict: Use Mole if you want a Mac CLI for inspecting storage and reviewing cleanup targets.
reviews.skip_if: Users who require every cleanup command to move files to Trash: clean, purge, and installer delete permanently.

reviews.name: swift
reviews.verdict: Our run passed 3 Python utility tests in 2 seconds, giving a clean result for utils/cmpcodesize/ and no compiler-wide test result.
reviews.skip_if: Web teams that cannot spend time replacing familiar delivery tools: Studioworks reports recreating build, deployment and chat tooling.

reviews.name: triton
reviews.verdict: Our Triton source install timed out after 900 seconds, with an editable-wheel log showing a failed CMake build.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a supported Windows or macOS deployment: the README lists Linux as the supported platform.

reviews.name: nx
reviews.verdict: Our Nx contributor checkout installed successfully, then build and test commands stopped during project-graph processing because the .NET plugin could not launch dotnet.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors expecting Node dependency installation to provide every required executable: our checkout could not launch dotnet.

reviews.name: terminal
reviews.verdict: Use Windows Terminal if you work on Windows and want configurable tabs around existing PowerShell, Command Prompt or WSL sessions.
reviews.skip_if: People seeking a native Linux or macOS terminal: the README requires Windows 10 2004, build 19041, or later.

reviews.name: intellij-community
reviews.verdict: Our IntelliJ sandbox passed 1,618 Rust helper tests, but it did not build or launch the full IDE.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who only need to use an IDE: this repository documents source builds and platform development.

reviews.name: nvm
reviews.verdict: Choose NVM for Windows for native Windows development when its documented shim or link mode matches your project workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring one manager across native Windows, macOS and Linux: fnm documents those platforms.

reviews.name: micro
reviews.verdict: Our micro run built in 47 seconds and passed all 12 recorded Go tests, making the source checkout worth a trial for familiar terminal editing.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring official Cygwin, MinGW or Plan 9 support: the README excludes those environments.

reviews.name: raylib
reviews.verdict: Our raylib install stopped after 6 seconds because CMake could not find the X11 include path and library required by its selected configuration.
reviews.skip_if: Desktop tools requiring several native windows: the README lists no multi-window support.

reviews.name: sentry
reviews.verdict: Use Sentry if your application team needs errors connected to frontend and backend debugging context.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who require demonstrated GitLab Autofix support before choosing a product: issue #93724 records that requirement and requests for a timeline.

reviews.name: beads
reviews.verdict: Beads built in 206 seconds in our sandbox, but its test step exited 1 with 17 failures in the supplied summary.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting simultaneous writers in the default embedded database: the README specifies a single writer.

reviews.name: rust
reviews.verdict: Our Rust checkout completed a 24-second Yarn install, but the compiler build and tests were skipped, so that result cannot validate the toolchain.
reviews.skip_if: Teams approving an entire Python migration solely for speed: one commenter reports weeks of work and growth from about 40,000 to 120,000 lines, without a performance result.

reviews.name: compound-engineering-plugin
reviews.verdict: Use a supervised trial if shared plans and repository lessons match your team's needs.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting lfg to stop after editing files: the README says it commits and, when a remote exists, pushes and opens a PR.

reviews.name: nuclei
reviews.verdict: Nuclei is worth a controlled trial for teams that will review templates and confirm findings.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting installation of the CLI to provide a ready-made shared scanning service: the README warns that service operation may pose security risks.

reviews.name: gastown
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Gas Town in a disposable repository when persistent assignments and merge coordination address a recurring problem.
reviews.skip_if: Developers whose existing assistant, worktrees and task list already cover their coordination needs Teams requiring a verified working installation and clean build before evaluation: our supplied record establishes neither Native Windows users expecting the full tmux-backed workflow in PowerShell; the…

reviews.name: esbuild
reviews.verdict: Our source build passed in 22 seconds and all 16 recorded Go tests passed in 13 seconds, which supports working on this checkout, not a claim about your application's bundling speed.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting TypeScript compilation to include type checking: esbuild leaves that job to tsc.

reviews.name: minikube
reviews.verdict: Our Minikube build succeeded in 198 seconds, but the test run failed with 119 passes and 17 failures out of 136 recorded results.
reviews.skip_if: Machines where a compatible container or virtual-machine manager cannot run: the getting-started guide requires one.

reviews.name: DefinitelyTyped
reviews.verdict: Our repository install failed after 89 seconds because npm hit an explicit pnpm requirement.
reviews.skip_if: TypeScript library authors who can ship generated declarations with their own package: the README recommends bundling them.

reviews.name: biome
reviews.verdict: Our Biome workspace install finished in 18 seconds; build and tests were skipped.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring unchanged ESLint behavior without comparing rule options and diagnostics.

reviews.name: slint
reviews.verdict: Slint's dependencies installed in 33 seconds in our sandbox, but the build and tests were skipped, leaving native UI operation unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a binding without a beta label for JavaScript or Python: the README marks both beta.

reviews.name: proliferate
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Proliferate if connecting agent conversations to branches addresses an existing coordination problem.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors expecting a Node-only source setup: the README also requires Rust and pnpm.

reviews.name: node
reviews.verdict: Choose Node.js for a JavaScript team's APIs and integrations dominated by I/O, using an LTS release and a routine for security updates.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting expensive JavaScript request callbacks to leave other clients unaffected.

reviews.name: free-for-dev
reviews.verdict: Use free-for-dev if you want hosted-service candidates and will compare their current terms.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for software to host themselves: the main list explicitly excludes self-hosted software.

reviews.name: security-audit-skill
reviews.verdict: Use security-audit-skill for bounded source investigations when your host supports parallel agents, execution has an enforced sandbox and a developer can review findings and fixes.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a predictable low-cost automatic release gate.

reviews.name: protobuf
reviews.verdict: Our Python install took 6 seconds and the build passed in 1 second, but tests were skipped and pip-audit reported 2 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need readable, loosely structured exchanges and want to avoid schema and code-generation upkeep.

reviews.name: open-code-review
reviews.verdict: Our published-package run installed v1.14.0 in 6.5 seconds, then provider setup failed because /dev/tty was unavailable.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing an immediately dependable merge gate: Wisk.aero reports missing gating features in its early CI rollout.

reviews.name: pulumi
reviews.verdict: The October 1, 2026 run at fd80abd passed 15 of 15 npm-project tests in 7 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting previews to automatically incorporate every manual cloud change without a refresh.

reviews.name: zx
reviews.verdict: Use zx when familiar JavaScript simplifies scripts combining shell commands with JSON or API calls, and your team can specify the shell and external executables.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting Bash commands to work unchanged in PowerShell: issue #523 reports PowerShell rejecting the -rf parameter.

reviews.name: cilium
reviews.verdict: Shortlist Cilium when its documented identity-based policy or Hubble visibility addresses a specific Kubernetes networking requirement.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring Windows worker networking: the supplied Cilium requirements specify Linux hosts with AMD64 or AArch64 architecture.

reviews.name: GitNexus
reviews.verdict: Our source-harness installation succeeded in 5 seconds, but the hands-on deployment hit our lab's bind-mount safety rule.

reviews.name: golangci-lint

reviews.skip_if: Teams selecting a dependable assistant on the strength of a training tutorial.

reviews.name: SillyTavern
reviews.verdict: Consider SillyTavern when lorebooks and prompt controls justify learning the interface and maintaining a separate backend.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a hosted chat account: the maintainers provide no online or hosted services.

reviews.name: langflow
reviews.verdict: Use Langflow when a shared visual workflow and Python customization justify operating its runtime.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking only for application code rather than a visual authoring environment and its runtime.

reviews.name: openinterpreter
reviews.verdict: Our pnpm install completed in 15 seconds, but the later hands-on attempt failed a Compose-file prerequisite before running a task.
reviews.skip_if: People following old Python computer-control tutorials who expect those commands to install the current Rust agent.

reviews.name: llm_wiki
reviews.verdict: Our llm_wiki sandbox install took 20 seconds and the build succeeded, but the test command exited 1 and a later Compose-required attempt stopped before a document task.
reviews.skip_if: Obsidian users requiring bidirectional synchronization: the maintainer describes vault import as copying and says that method cannot synchronize both ways.

reviews.name: heretic
reviews.verdict: Use Heretic if you want control over model modification and can evaluate the resulting answers yourself.
reviews.skip_if: Readers requiring guaranteed preservation of reasoning or answer quality.

reviews.name: eino
reviews.verdict: Eino passed all 90 recorded Go tests in our sandbox, with an 8-second install and a 52-second build, which supports trying it inside a Go service.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a ready-to-run end-user assistant: the README demonstrates constructing agents and tools in Go code.

reviews.name: promptfoo
reviews.verdict: Our Promptfoo run recorded 2,334 dependencies and 3,190 MB, then failed its source build and test commands, so contributors should reproduce those failures before relying on that workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a clean source build before adoption: our measured build and test commands both exited 1.

reviews.name: awesome-llm-apps
reviews.verdict: Use Awesome LLM Apps if you can inspect Python and want a particular application starter.
reviews.skip_if: Teams buying a supported deployment across the application catalog.

reviews.name: awesome-agent-skills
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox assessment produced no linked-skill result, while issue #971 records a concrete curation fix: 155 stale NVIDIA links replaced with one maintained catalog link.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need inclusion to certify a security audit: VoltAgent explicitly disclaims that guarantee.

reviews.name: nanoGPT
reviews.verdict: Use nanoGPT to study or modify Karpathy's compact PyTorch training implementation, with responsibility for your own fork and experiment configuration.
reviews.skip_if: Developers choosing a new project that depends on ongoing upstream development: the README recommends nanochat.

reviews.name: 9router
reviews.verdict: Our 9Router source build succeeded in 96 seconds, but npm audit reported 7 high-severity findings and our run found no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Operators expecting safe public exposure from copied defaults: the README defaults API-key enforcement and secure auth cookies to false.

reviews.name: langfuse
reviews.verdict: Use Langfuse if your application team needs tracing, prompt management and evaluations together and has a suitable hosting owner.
reviews.skip_if: Teams choosing self-hosting without an owner for storage and [database recovery](research:a552e0532b650ab3#issue-12172).

reviews.name: LightRAG
reviews.verdict: Use LightRAG if you can operate its model services, inspect retrieved evidence and compare graph-assisted answers with a simpler baseline.
reviews.skip_if: Teams buying a ready-made legal update workflow for current and superseded provisions.

reviews.name: llmfit
reviews.verdict: Use AlexsJones/llmfit to choose candidates for an existing computer and runtime.
reviews.skip_if: People whose selection depends on Ryzen AI, Intel AI Boost or Qualcomm Hexagon NPU detection, which issue #301 describes as absent.

reviews.name: opencode
reviews.verdict: OpenCode's archived Go checkout installed in 111 seconds and built in 72 seconds in our sandbox, then its test command failed.
reviews.skip_if: New production deployments: the repository is archived and its README warns that it is not ready for production use.

reviews.name: OpenViking
reviews.verdict: Our OpenViking source run installed in 60 seconds and built in 6 seconds, then tests stopped on a missing pytest_asyncio import.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need local-model extraction to work without checking stored additions: issue #3508 contains reproductions of successful-looking tasks with empty operations.

reviews.name: dspy
reviews.verdict: Our October DSPy source run installed in 55 seconds and completed its test step in 805 seconds with zero reported failures, alongside 584 skips and 2 audit vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: A stable single-call task that already works with a reviewed prompt and regression evaluations: the extra search workflow may buy you little.

reviews.name: hindsight
reviews.verdict: Use Hindsight if you want persistent agent memory and can inspect retained facts, refine selection rules and monitor writes separately from recall.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who require dependable unattended capture: OpenClaw issue #4828 reports recall continuing while new writes stop.

reviews.name: freellmapi
reviews.verdict: Our November Docker run failed its health step after 603 seconds because the required encryption key was missing; the earlier source run passed 3,950 tests.
reviews.skip_if: Customer-facing chatbots requiring dependable inference: the project explicitly recommends a paid API before shipping.

reviews.name: airllm
reviews.verdict: Use AirLLM for experiments with a chosen checkpoint that exceeds available GPU memory, when waiting minutes for output still serves the task.
reviews.skip_if: People choosing a runtime for a responsive chat assistant: Rocky Tested reported 0.1769 tokens/s for its Qwen3.5-9B experiment.

reviews.name: continue
reviews.verdict: Use Continue if an existing configuration earns its place and someone can own its maintenance.
reviews.skip_if: New teams requiring upstream maintenance: the README says active maintenance has ended.

reviews.name: reverse-skill
reviews.verdict: Use reverse-skill if you already judge security-tool output and want the explicit routing, evidence and same-step retry requirements documented in its README and issue #65.
reviews.skip_if: Teams buying a guarantee against provider refusals or account restrictions: issue #63 places those decisions under provider policy.

reviews.name: dify
reviews.verdict: Choose Dify when colleagues need shared visual editing of prompts, retrieval and routing, and someone can own deployment.
reviews.skip_if: Businesses requiring unrestricted customer-workspace hosting or frontend rebranding under the supplied license.

reviews.name: llama_index
reviews.verdict: Use LlamaIndex when document-heavy retrieval justifies maintaining parser, model and storage choices.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose simple retrieval code or mature custom service already meets their needs.

reviews.name: langchain
reviews.verdict: Use LangChain when reusable model interfaces, integrations and a configurable tool loop replace code your Python team would otherwise maintain.
reviews.skip_if: Developers making a bounded model call: LangChain's own comparison recommends starting with the direct model API.

reviews.name: llama.cpp
reviews.verdict: Choose llama.cpp when direct control over model files, quantization and execution settings justifies evaluating your own workload.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners whose immediate priority is learning model controls through a desktop GUI; the cited LM Studio user recommends its visual interface for that purpose.

reviews.name: nier-reincarnation-pc
reviews.verdict: Our Go server build succeeded in 65 seconds, while tests failed after 29 seconds with 24 passes and 1 failure recorded.
reviews.skip_if: Players requiring dependable Proton gameplay: issue #9 reports a 40% loading stall after the 1.3.1 crash fix.

reviews.name: unikraft-xray-node
reviews.verdict: Use unikraft-xray-node for a technical experiment with Unikraft-specific WS/XHTTP routing and generated client files.
reviews.skip_if: Users choosing a daily connection on the strength of this review's deployment result.

reviews.name: datacat
reviews.verdict: Use DataCat for a separate self-hosted monitoring evaluation alongside existing alerts.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose adoption decision requires demonstrated full Datadog replacement coverage.

reviews.name: prusa-connect
reviews.verdict: Our build passed in 88 seconds, but our test command failed after 388 seconds with two upgrade-process failures.
reviews.skip_if: MK3S owners expecting their existing PrusaLink HTTP connection to work with Local: issue #9 describes that path as unsupported.

reviews.name: lastbook
reviews.verdict: Our Lastbook packaging run installed in 6 seconds and built in 1 second, with tests skipped because no test target was detected.
reviews.skip_if: E-reader users who want public, individual PDF or EPUB downloads: issue #270 keeps that workflow open.

reviews.name: freebie-radar
reviews.verdict: Our pnpm install failed in 12 seconds, and a separate Docker attempt stopped at the image pull.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners expecting an upstream image they can simply pull: our deployment stopped at pull access denied, and issue #7's image request ends with a wait-for-refactor reply.

reviews.name: panel
reviews.verdict: Our npm install completed in 24 seconds, but the build failed in 3 seconds and the deployment attempt stopped at its Compose safety check.
reviews.skip_if: Operators requiring a released whole-machine migration workflow: issue #104 is an open proposal.

reviews.name: PeakCut
reviews.verdict: Our run installed PeakCut in 5 seconds and built it in 1 second, but pytest stopped with a collection/setup error.
reviews.skip_if: Creators whose immediate requirement is Instagram connection through a new Meta app offering only Unified login or Facebook login.

reviews.name: tinytraffic
reviews.verdict: Our tinytraffic source build failed after 21 seconds and the test command stopped at Go manifest parsing after 2 seconds, so our run supports a setup warning rather than a working-service recommendation.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who require uninterrupted rolling updates while keeping the default DuckDB file: its documented deployment requires stop-first updates.

reviews.name: mygo-music
reviews.verdict: Use MyGo Music if you want local files in a native desktop player and can choose a plugin around its documented audio source and account features.
reviews.skip_if: Spotify listeners who require direct Spotify audio: MyGotify uses YouTube Music audio.

reviews.name: hermes-voice
reviews.verdict: Use majorminorlabs/hermes-voice if you already operate Home Assistant and Hermes and want an Assist device connected to a deliberately configured voice profile.
reviews.skip_if: Households requiring private memories for each speaker: the documented memory boundary is the profile.

reviews.name: TREK
reviews.verdict: Use TREK if owning the planning server is worth maintaining Docker, HTTPS and integration credentials.
reviews.skip_if: Travellers who want a hosted planning service without container and reverse-proxy administration.

reviews.name: open-orange
reviews.verdict: Our build completed in 2 seconds, but the tests timed out at 900 seconds and the separate CLI recipe stopped before running an application.
reviews.skip_if: Platforms relying on Worker Loader CPU and subrequest limits to contain untrusted user code: issue #58 reports those limits are ignored.

reviews.name: homelab-diagram
reviews.verdict: Use Goblinmine/homelab-diagram if you want its detailed port, VLAN and server-card style and can maintain Python coordinates alongside YAML.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing automatic layout for arbitrary inventories: the README describes coordinates tailored to one network.

reviews.name: StudyOnTV
reviews.verdict: Our parent-UI run passed installation in 22 seconds, build in 21 seconds and tests in 10 seconds, while a Huawei household reported both successful quiz unlocking and a power-button bypass.
reviews.skip_if: Households needing unattended enforcement after power-button use: the Huawei v0.4.2 reporter documented a bypass.

reviews.name: offline-emergency-library
reviews.verdict: Contributor tests show working US browser maps on Windows and cited manual answers on Linux arm64 in a VM; our lab attempt stopped before application execution.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing an emergency appliance already qualified on their exact hardware: the detailed Linux reader reports use VMs.

reviews.name: hypergrad
reviews.verdict: Our HyperGrad Docker deployment failed at an image pull, and the separate sandbox suite reported 9 passed and 1 failed test.
